1	\section{Sawtooth sums and the main term for one modulus}\label{sec:sawtooth}
     2	
     3	\subsection{Sawtooth sums}
     4	
     5	The function $B(u)=\fr u(1-\fr u)$ is continuous, $1$-periodic, takes values in $[0,\frac14]$, and satisfies $B(u)=u-u^2$ for $0\le u\le1$. The sums we need are $\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)$ and weighted versions of them. Their size $\asymp\sqrt Z$ has two sources: the terms with $s>\sqrt Z$, where $B(Z/s^2)=Z/s^2-Z^2/s^4$, and the terms with $s\le\sqrt Z$, where $B$ oscillates. The natural approximation is the integral $\int_0^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du=I\sqrt Z$ (substitute $u=\sqrt Z\,w$). For $q\in\N$ put
     6	\[
     7	\kappa_q(t)=\kappa(t)\one[(t,q)=1],\qquad \Delta_q=\prod_p\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\one[p\nmid q]\frac{p}{p^2-2}\Bigr).
     8	\]
     9	For $p\nmid q$ the factor of $\Delta_q$ is $(p-1)^2(p+2)/(p(p^2-2))=1+O(p^{-2})$; there are finitely many other factors, so the product converges absolutely.
    10	
    11	\begin{proposition}[Sawtooth sums]\label{prop:sawtooth}
    12	\leavevmode
    13	\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
    14	\item $I=\int_0^\infty B(u^{-2})\,du=\frac12\int_0^\infty B(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=-4\zeta(-\tfrac12)$.
    15	\item For every real $Z>0$, $\bigl|\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z\bigr|\le c_1Z^{1/3}$ with $c_1=60$.
    16	\item For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_5(\eps)$ such that for all $q\in\N$ and real $Z>0$,
    17	\[
    18	\Bigl|\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-\Delta_q\,I\sqrt Z\Bigr|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^\eps Z^{1/3}.
    19	\]
    20	\end{enumerate}
    21	\end{proposition}
    22	
    23	\begin{proof}
    24	(a) The substitution $v=u^{-2}$ gives the second expression. The integral converges, because $B(v)\le v$ near $0$ and $B(v)\le\frac14$. Since $B$ is continuous and piecewise $C^1$ with $B'(v)=1-2\fr v$, integration by parts on $[0,X]$ gives
    25	\[
    26	\int_0^XB(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=\bigl[-2B(v)v^{-1/2}\bigr]_0^X+2\int_0^XB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv .
    27	\]
    28	The boundary term tends to $0$, because $B(v)v^{-1/2}\le v^{1/2}$ near $0$ and $B(X)X^{-1/2}\le\frac14X^{-1/2}$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=2\lim_{N\to\infty}\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv$ along integers $N$. On $(n,n+1)$ we have $B'(n^+)=1$, $B'((n+1)^-)=-1$ and $B''=-2$, so integrating by parts with the antiderivative $2v^{1/2}$ of $v^{-1/2}$,
    29	\[
    30	\int_n^{n+1}B'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-2(n+1)^{1/2}-2n^{1/2}+4\int_n^{n+1}v^{1/2}\,dv,
    31	\]
    32	and summing over $0\le n<N$,
    33	\begin{equation}\label{eq:Bprime}
    34	\int_0^NB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-4\sum_{m=1}^Nm^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+\tfrac83N^{3/2}.
    35	\end{equation}
    36	Now apply \cref{lem:EM} on $(N,\infty)$ to $G(u)=u^{-s}$ with $\Re s>1$, using $\psi(N)=-\frac12$ and $\psi_2(N)=\frac1{12}$:
    37	\[
    38	\sum_{n>N}n^{-s}=\frac{N^{1-s}}{s-1}-\frac{N^{-s}}2+\frac s{12}N^{-s-1}-s(s+1)\int_N^\infty\psi_2(u)u^{-s-2}\,du .
    39	\]
    40	The right-hand side is analytic in $\Re s>-1$, $s\ne1$, because the integral converges locally uniformly there. By uniqueness of analytic continuation, $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le N}n^{-s}$ plus the right-hand side in that region. At $s=-\frac12$ we have $s(s+1)=-\frac14$ and $|\int_N^\infty\psi_2u^{-3/2}\,du|\le\frac16N^{-1/2}$, so
    41	\[
    42	\sum_{m\le N}m^{1/2}=\zeta(-\tfrac12)+\tfrac23N^{3/2}+\tfrac12N^{1/2}+O(N^{-1/2}).
    43	\]
    44	Inserting this into~\eqref{eq:Bprime} shows that $\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv\to-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=-8\zeta(-\frac12)$ and $I=-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. By the functional equation~\cite[Corollary~10.4]{MV2007} at $s=-\frac12$, $\zeta(-\frac12)=2^{-1/2}\pi^{-3/2}\Gamma(\frac32)\sin(-\frac\pi4)\zeta(\frac32)=-\zeta(\frac32)/(4\pi)$. So $I=\zeta(3/2)/\pi>0$, the value stated in~\eqref{eq:I}.
    45	
    46	(b) \emph{The case $Z<1$.} Here $0\le B(Z/s^2)\le Z/s^2$, so $0\le\sum_sB(Z/s^2)\le\zeta(2)Z<2Z^{1/3}$. Also $0<I\sqrt Z<Z^{1/3}$, since $I<1$. The difference of two numbers in $[0,2Z^{1/3}]$ is at most $2Z^{1/3}$.
    47	
    48	\emph{The case $Z\ge1$.} Put $\Lambda=Z^{1/3}\ge1$ and $T=\lfloor\Lambda\rfloor\ge1$. Then $\Lambda/2<T\le\Lambda$, hence
    49	\begin{equation}\label{eq:b1}
    50	\frac Z{T^3}<8,\qquad K_0:=\frac Z{T^2}<4\Lambda,\qquad \frac{Z^2}{T^5}<32\Lambda .
    51	\end{equation}
    52	\emph{Small $s$.} Both $\sum_{s\le T}B(Z/s^2)$ and $\int_0^TB(Z/u^2)\,du$ lie in $[0,T/4]\subset[0,\Lambda/4]$, so their difference is at most $\Lambda/4$. It therefore suffices to show
    53	\begin{equation}\label{eq:b2}
    54	\Bigl|\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)-\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du\Bigr|\le57\Lambda ,
    55	\end{equation}
    56	which gives the claim with $57+\frac14<60$.
    57	
    58	\emph{A decomposition of $B$.} For real $w\ge0$ with $j=\lfloor w\rfloor$ we have $B(w)=(w-j)(1-w+j)=w-w^2+2jw-j-j^2$, and $\sum_{k=1}^j2(w-k)=2jw-j^2-j$. Hence
    59	\[
    60	B(w)=w-w^2+2\sum_{k\ge1}(w-k)_+,\qquad(v)_+=\max(v,0).
    61	\]
    62	Put $\Phi(u)=Z/u^2-Z^2/u^4$ and $G_k(u)=(Z/u^2-k)_+$, so that $B(Z/u^2)=\Phi(u)+2\sum_{k\ge1}G_k(u)$. For $u\ge T$ only the $k<K_0$ contribute, and there are fewer than $K_0<4\Lambda$ of them. For such $k$, $G_k(u)=Z/u^2-k$ on $[T,R_k]$ with $R_k=\sqrt{Z/k}>T$, and $G_k=0$ on $[R_k,\infty)$.
    63	
    64	\emph{Euler--Maclaurin.} Apply \cref{lem:EM} to $\Phi$ on $(T,\infty)$, and to $Z/u^2-k$ on $(T,R_k]$ for each $k<K_0$. Use $\psi(T)=-\frac12$, $\psi_2(T)=\frac1{12}$ and $G_k(R_k)=0$, and add. Since $\int_T^\infty\Phi+2\sum_k\int_T^{R_k}G_k=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du$ (all integrals converge absolutely), this gives
    65	\[
    66	\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du+R_1+R_2+R_3+R_4+R_5,
    67	\]
    68	where, writing $G_k'$ and $G_k''$ for the derivatives of $Z/u^2-k$:
    69	\begin{itemize}
    70	\item $R_1=\psi(T)\bigl[\Phi(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k(T)\bigr]=\psi(T)B(Z/T^2)$. The individual terms here have size about $Z^2/T^4\asymp Z^{2/3}$, but their sum is $B(Z/T^2)\le\frac14$. So $|R_1|\le\frac18$. This is the one place where cancellation is essential.
    71	\item $R_2=-\frac1{12}\bigl[\Phi'(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k'(T)\bigr]$, with $\Phi'(T)=-2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5$ and $G_k'(T)=-2Z/T^3$. By~\eqref{eq:b1}, $|\Phi'(T)|<16+128\Lambda$ and $|2\sum_kG_k'(T)|\le4K_0Z/T^3<128\Lambda$. So $|R_2|\le\frac1{12}(16+256\Lambda)\le\frac{272}{12}\Lambda$.
    72	\item $R_3=-\int_T^\infty\psi_2\Phi''\,du$ with $\Phi''=6Z/u^4-20Z^2/u^6$. So $|R_3|\le\frac1{12}(2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5)<\frac1{12}(16+128\Lambda)\le12\Lambda$.
    73	\item $R_4=-2\sum_{k<K_0}\int_T^{R_k}\psi_2G_k''\,du$ with $G_k''=6Z/u^4$ and $\int_T^\infty6Zu^{-4}\,du=2Z/T^3<16$. So $|R_4|\le\frac2{12}K_0\cdot16<\frac{32}3\Lambda$.
    74	\item $R_5=2\sum_{k<K_0}\psi_2(R_k)G_k'(R_k)$ with $G_k'(R_k)=-2Z/R_k^3=-2k^{3/2}/\sqrt Z$. Since $k<4\Lambda$, $\sum_{k<K_0}k^{3/2}<4\Lambda\cdot8\Lambda^{3/2}$, and with $\sqrt Z=\Lambda^{3/2}$ we get $|R_5|\le\frac2{12}\cdot2\cdot32\Lambda=\frac{32}3\Lambda$. These are the kinks of the $G_k$ at the points $R_k$. Summing over the $K_0\asymp Z^{1/3}$ values of $k$ is what produces the exponent $\frac13$.
    75	\end{itemize}
    76	Using $\Lambda\ge1$, the total is at most $(\frac18+\frac{272}{12}+12+\frac{32}3+\frac{32}3)\Lambda=\frac{449}8\Lambda<57\Lambda$, which proves~\eqref{eq:b2}.
    77	
    78	(c) Fix $q$. The function $\kappa_q$ is multiplicative with $\kappa_q(p)=p^2/(p^2-2)$ for $p\nmid q$, $\kappa_q(p)=0$ for $p\mid q$ and $\kappa_q(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$. Let $\beta=\mu*\kappa_q$, so that $\kappa_q=1*\beta$. Then $\beta$ is multiplicative, with $\beta(p^j)=\kappa_q(p^j)-\kappa_q(p^{j-1})$:
    79	\begin{itemize}
    80	\item for $p\mid q$: $\beta(p)=-1$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$;
    81	\item for $p\nmid q$: $\beta(p)=\frac2{p^2-2}$, $\beta(p^2)=-\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge3$.
    82	\end{itemize}
    83	\emph{Absolute convergence.} For $p\nmid q$, $\sum_j|\beta(p^j)|p^{-2j/3}\le\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}$, because $p^2/(p^2-2)\le2$. Hence
    84	\[
    85	\Sigma_{2/3}:=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{|\beta(n)|}{n^{2/3}}\le\prod_{p\mid q}\bigl(1+p^{-2/3}\bigr)\prod_p\Bigl(1+\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}\Bigr)\le C_\beta\,2^{\omega(q)}\le C_\beta C(\eps)q^\eps,
    86	\]
    87	with an absolute constant $C_\beta$, by \cref{lem:divisor}. Similarly $\sum_n|\beta(n)|/n<\infty$ for each fixed $q$.
    88	
    89	\emph{Rearrangement.} For $W>0$, $\sum_mB(W/m^2)\le\sum_m\min(\frac14,W/m^2)\le3\sqrt W$. Indeed, for $W<1$ the sum is at most $\zeta(2)W\le2\sqrt W$, and for $W\ge1$ it is at most $\frac14\sqrt W+W\cdot2/\sqrt W$ by \cref{lem:tail}. Hence $\sum_{n,m}|\beta(n)|B(Z/(nm)^2)\le3\sqrt Z\sum_n|\beta(n)|/n<\infty$, and we may rearrange:
    90	\[
    91	\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)=\sum_{n,m\ge1}\beta(n)B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr)=\sum_{n\ge1}\beta(n)\sum_{m\ge1}B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr).
    92	\]
    93	\emph{Main term.} Part (b) holds for every positive argument. Applying it with $Z/n^2$ in place of $Z$, and using $I\sqrt{Z/n^2}=I\sqrt Z/n$,
    94	\[
    95	\Bigl|\sum_t\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-I\sqrt Z\sum_n\frac{\beta(n)}n\Bigr|\le c_1\sum_n|\beta(n)|\Bigl(\frac Z{n^2}\Bigr)^{1/3}=c_1\Sigma_{2/3}Z^{1/3}.
    96	\]
    97	\emph{The constant.} By~\eqref{eq:euler}, $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\prod_p\bigl(1+\beta(p)/p+\beta(p^2)/p^2\bigr)$. For $p\mid q$ the factor is $1-1/p$. For $p\nmid q$ it is
    98	\[
    99	1+\frac2{p(p^2-2)}-\frac1{p^2-2}=\frac{p^3-3p+2}{p(p^2-2)}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p(p^2-2)}=\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\frac p{p^2-2}\Bigr).
   100	\]
   101	Hence $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\Delta_q$, and (c) holds with $c_5(\eps)=c_1C_\beta C(\eps)$.
   102	\end{proof}
   103	
   104	\subsection{The main term for one modulus}
   105	
   106	\begin{proposition}[Asymptotics of $\MT$]\label{prop:MT}
   107	For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_6(\eps)$ such that for all real $x>0$ and all $q\in\N$,
   108	\[
   109	\bigl|\MT(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}\bigr|\le c_6(\eps)\,x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps},
   110	\]
   111	with $h$ as in~\eqref{eq:h}. In particular this holds for $x\ge1$ and $1\le q\le x$.
   112	\end{proposition}
   113	
   114	\begin{proof}
   115	\emph{Factorising $t$.} Fix $q$. Every squarefree $t$ factors uniquely as $t=t_0t_1t_2$, where $t_0$ is composed of primes $p\nmid q$, $t_1$ of primes $p\,\|\,q$, and $t_2$ of primes $p$ with $p^2\mid q$. Conversely, every such triple of squarefree numbers gives a squarefree $t$. Let $\mathcal S_1$ and $\mathcal S_2$ be the finite sets of admissible $t_1$ and $t_2$ (all of them divide $q$). For squarefree $t$, $\gcd(t^2,q)=\prod_{p\mid t}p^{\min(2,v_p(q))}=t_1t_2^2$, so
   116	\[
   117	m_t(q)=t_0^2t_1,\qquad\frac x{q\,m_t(q)}=\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\quad\text{with}\quad Z_1=\frac{x}{q\,t_1},\qquad \eta(t)m_t(q)=\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\kappa(t_0).
   118	\]
   119	By the absolute convergence in \cref{lem:eta} we may regroup:
   120	\[
   121	\MT(x;q)=A_0\,q\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\Sigma(t_1),\qquad\Sigma(t_1)=\sum_{t_0\ge1}\kappa_q(t_0)B\Bigl(\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\Bigr).
   122	\]
   123	\emph{Applying \cref{prop:sawtooth}(c).} With $Z=Z_1>0$ we get $\Sigma(t_1)=\Delta_qI\sqrt{Z_1}+\theta\,c_5(\eps)q^\eps Z_1^{1/3}$. Since $t_1\sqrt{Z_1}=\sqrt{x/q}\,t_1^{1/2}$ and $t_1Z_1^{1/3}=(x/q)^{1/3}t_1^{2/3}$,
   124	\[
   125	\MT(x;q)=A_0\Delta_qI\sqrt{xq}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)+R,
   126	\]
   127	\[
   128	|R|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^{1+\eps}\Bigl(\frac xq\Bigr)^{1/3}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2),
   129	\]
   130	where we used $A_0\le1$. By~\eqref{eq:eta-bound}, $\sum_{t_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-4/3})$ and $\sum_{t_2}\eta(t_2)\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-2})$, both absolute constants. So $|R|\le c_6(\eps)x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}$.
   131	
   132	\emph{The constant is $h(q)$.} The two finite sums are Euler products over the primes dividing $q$:
   133	\[
   134	\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}=\prod_{p\|q}\Bigl(1+\frac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr),\qquad\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)=\prod_{p^2\mid q}\Bigl(1+\frac1{p^2-2}\Bigr).
   135	\]
   136	Multiplying the absolutely convergent products $A_0$ and $\Delta_q$ factor by factor, the local factor at $p$ of the main coefficient is
   137	\begin{align*}
   138	p\nmid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac p{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2+p-2)}{p^3}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p^3}=a_p,\\
   139	p\,\|\,q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-2+\sqrt p)}{p^3}=b_p,\\
   140	p^2\mid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac1{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-1)}{p^3}=c_p .
   141	\end{align*}
   142	Together with the factor $I$, this is exactly $h(q)$.
   143	\end{proof}
   144	
   145	\begin{remark}
   146	Since $b_p/a_p\ge1-1/p$ and $c_p/a_p=(p+1)/(p+2)\ge1-1/p$, we have $h(q)\ge IA_h\,\varphi(q)/q\gg_\eps q^{-\eps}$, where $A_h=\prod_pa_p>0$ (\cref{prop:poly}(0)). So \cref{prop:MT} gives $\MT(x;q)=h(q)\sqrt{xq}\,\bigl(1+O_\eps(x^{2\eps}(q/x)^{1/6})\bigr)$. The relative error is not small when $q\asymp x$. This is why the asymptotic formula of \cref{thm:main}(iii) requires $Y\le x^{1-\delta}$, whereas the error term in~(ii), which keeps $\MT$ unexpanded, has no such restriction. The numerical data in \cref{sec:numerics} suggest that, after summation over the moduli, the secondary term has relative size roughly proportional to $\sqrt{Y/x}$. That is consistent with, but sharper than, the proved bound.
   147	\end{remark}
\section{The variance for a single modulus}\label{sec:single}

\begin{proposition}[Single-modulus variance]\label{prop:single}
For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_7(\eps)$ such that for all real $x\ge2$ and all integers $1\le q\le x$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $|V(x;q)-\MT(x;q)|\le c_7(\eps)\bigl(x^{5/3+\eps}/q+\sqrt x\bigr)$;
\item $|V(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}|\le c_7(\eps)\bigl(x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}+x^{5/3+\eps}/q+\sqrt x\bigr)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) By \cref{prop:identity}, which holds for all $x\ge1$ and $q\in\N$,
\[
V(x;q)-\MT(x;q)=2\sum_{1\le h\le x/q}D_x(hq)+\Bigl(Q(x)-\frac{6x}{\pi^2}\Bigr)-2x\sum_{l=1}^qg(q,l)E(x;q,l).
\]
For $1\le h\le x/q$ the integer $m=hq$ satisfies $1\le m\le x$. Since $x\ge2$, \cref{prop:pairs} applies to each of the at most $x/q$ terms. (This is the only place where $x\ge2$ rather than $x\ge1$ is needed.) It gives
\[
\Bigl|2\sum_{1\le h\le x/q}D_x(hq)\Bigr|\le2\cdot\frac xq\cdot c_3(\eps)x^{2/3+\eps}=2c_3(\eps)\frac{x^{5/3+\eps}}q .
\]
\Cref{prop:trivial}(i) gives $|Q(x)-6x/\pi^2|\le c_0\sqrt x$. \Cref{prop:trivial}(ii) gives
\[
\Bigl|2x\sum_lg(q,l)E(x;q,l)\Bigr|\le2c_0\frac{x^{3/2}}q\le2c_0\frac{x^{5/3+\eps}}q,
\]
since $x\ge1$. By the triangle inequality, (i) holds with $c_7(\eps)\ge2c_3(\eps)+2c_0$.

(ii) \Cref{prop:MT} gives $|\MT(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}|\le c_6(\eps)x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}$. Combining this with (i) by the triangle inequality proves (ii) with
\[
c_7(\eps)=\max\bigl\{2c_3(\eps)+2c_0,\ c_6(\eps)\bigr\},
\]
and (i) remains true with this larger constant.
\end{proof}

    11	\begin{proposition}[Sawtooth sums]\label{prop:sawtooth}
    12	\leavevmode
    13	\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
    14	\item $I=\int_0^\infty B(u^{-2})\,du=\frac12\int_0^\infty B(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=-4\zeta(-\tfrac12)$.

    25	\[
    26	\int_0^XB(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=\bigl[-2B(v)v^{-1/2}\bigr]_0^X+2\int_0^XB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv .

    29	\[
    30	\int_n^{n+1}B'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-2(n+1)^{1/2}-2n^{1/2}+4\int_n^{n+1}v^{1/2}\,dv,
    31	\]

    34	\int_0^NB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-4\sum_{m=1}^Nm^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+\tfrac83N^{3/2}.
    35	\end{equation}
    36	Now apply \cref{lem:EM} on $(N,\infty)$ to $G(u)=u^{-s}$ with $\Re s>1$, using $\psi(N)=-\frac12$ and $\psi_2(N)=\frac1{12}$:
    37	\[

    39	\]

    41	\[
    42	\sum_{m\le N}m^{1/2}=\zeta(-\tfrac12)+\tfrac23N^{3/2}+\tfrac12N^{1/2}+O(N^{-1/2}).
    43	\]

    47	
    48	\emph{The case $Z\ge1$.} Put $\Lambda=Z^{1/3}\ge1$ and $T=\lfloor\Lambda\rfloor\ge1$. Then $\Lambda/2<T\le\Lambda$, hence
    49	\begin{equation}\label{eq:b1}
    50	\frac Z{T^3}<8,\qquad K_0:=\frac Z{T^2}<4\Lambda,\qquad \frac{Z^2}{T^5}<32\Lambda .
    51	\end{equation}

    58	\emph{A decomposition of $B$.} For real $w\ge0$ with $j=\lfloor w\rfloor$ we have $B(w)=(w-j)(1-w+j)=w-w^2+2jw-j-j^2$, and $\sum_{k=1}^j2(w-k)=2jw-j^2-j$. Hence

    64	\emph{Euler--Maclaurin.} Apply \cref{lem:EM} to $\Phi$ on $(T,\infty)$, and to $Z/u^2-k$ on $(T,R_k]$ for each $k<K_0$.     75	\end{itemize}
    76	Using $\Lambda\ge1$, the total is at most $(\frac18+\frac{272}{12}+12+\frac{32}3+\frac{32}3)\Lambda=\frac{449}8\Lambda<57\Lambda$, which proves~\eqref{eq:b2}.
    77	
    78	(c) Fix $q$. The function $\kappa_q$ is multiplicative with $\kappa_q(p)=p^2/(p^2-2)$ for $p\nmid q$, $\kappa_q(p)=0$ for $p\mid q$ and $\kappa_q(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$. Let $\beta=\mu*\kappa_q$, so that $\kappa_q=1*\beta$. Then $\beta$ is multiplicative, with $\beta(p^j)=\kappa_q(p^j)-\kappa_q(p^{j-1})$:
    79	\begin{itemize}
    80	\item for $p\mid q$: $\beta(p)=-1$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$;
    81	\item for $p\nmid q$: $\beta(p)=\frac2{p^2-2}$, $\beta(p^2)=-\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge3$.
    82	\end{itemize}

    85	\Sigma_{2/3}:=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{|\beta(n)|}{n^{2/3}}\le\prod_{p\mid q}\bigl(1+p^{-2/3}\bigr)\prod_p\Bigl(1+\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}\Bigr)\le C_\beta\,2^{\omega(q)}\le C_\beta C(\eps)q^\eps,

    98	\[
    99	1+\frac2{p(p^2-2)}-\frac1{p^2-2}=\frac{p^3-3p+2}{p(p^2-2)}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p(p^2-2)}=\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\frac p{p^2-2}\Bigr).

   102	\end{proof}

   104	\subsection{The main term for one modulus}

   106	\begin{proposition}[Asymptotics of $\MT$]\label{prop:MT}
   107	For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_6(\eps)$ such that for all real $x>0$ and all $q\in\N$,
   108	\[
   109	\bigl|\MT(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}\bigr|\le c_6(\eps)\,x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps},
   110	\]
   111	with $h$ as in~\eqref{eq:h}. In particular this holds for $x\ge1$ and $1\le q\le x$.
   112	\end{proposition}
   113	
   114	\begin{proof}
   115	\emph{Factorising $t$.} Fix $q$. Every squarefree $t$ factors uniquely as $t=t_0t_1t_2$, where $t_0$ is composed of primes $p\nmid q$, $t_1$ of primes $p\,\|\,q$, and $t_2$ of primes $p$ with $p^2\mid q$. Conversely, every such triple of squarefree numbers gives a squarefree $t$. Let $\mathcal S_1$ and $\mathcal S_2$ be the finite sets of admissible $t_1$ and $t_2$ (all of them divide $q$). For squarefree $t$, $\gcd(t^2,q)=\prod_{p\mid t}p^{\min(2,v_p(q))}=t_1t_2^2$, so
   116	\[
   117	m_t(q)=t_0^2t_1,\qquad\frac x{q\,m_t(q)}=\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\quad\text{with}\quad Z_1=\frac{x}{q\,t_1},\qquad \eta(t)m_t(q)=\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\kappa(t_0).
   118	\]
   119	By the absolute convergence in \cref{lem:eta} we may regroup:
   120	\[
   121	\MT(x;q)=A_0\,q\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\Sigma(t_1),\qquad\Sigma(t_1)=\sum_{t_0\ge1}\kappa_q(t_0)B\Bigl(\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\Bigr).
   122	\]
   123	\emph{Applying \cref{prop:sawtooth}(c).} With $Z=Z_1>0$ we get $\Sigma(t_1)=\Delta_qI\sqrt{Z_1}+\theta\,c_5(\eps)q^\eps Z_1^{1/3}$. Since $t_1\sqrt{Z_1}=\sqrt{x/q}\,t_1^{1/2}$ and $t_1Z_1^{1/3}=(x/q)^{1/3}t_1^{2/3}$,
   124	\[
   125	\MT(x;q)=A_0\Delta_qI\sqrt{xq}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)+R,
   126	\]
   127	\[
   128	|R|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^{1+\eps}\Bigl(\frac xq\Bigr)^{1/3}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2),
   129	\]
   130	where we used $A_0\le1$. By~\eqref{eq:eta-bound}, $\sum_{t_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-4/3})$ and $\sum_{t_2}\eta(t_2)\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-2})$, both absolute constants. So $|R|\le c_6(\eps)x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}$.
   131	
   132	\emph{The constant is $h(q)$.} The two finite sums are Euler products over the primes dividing $q$:
   133	\[
   134	\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}=\prod_{p\|q}\Bigl(1+\frac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr),\qquad\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)=\prod_{p^2\mid q}\Bigl(1+\frac1{p^2-2}\Bigr).
   135	\]
   136	Multiplying the absolutely convergent products $A_0$ and $\Delta_q$ factor by factor, the local factor at $p$ of the main coefficient is
   137	\begin{align*}
   138	p\nmid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac p{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2+p-2)}{p^3}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p^3}=a_p,\\
   139	p\,\|\,q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-2+\sqrt p)}{p^3}=b_p,\\
   140	p^2\mid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac1{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-1)}{p^3}=c_p .
   141	\end{align*}
   142	Together with the factor $I$, this is exactly $h(q)$.
   143	\end{proof}
   144	
   145	\begin{remark}
   146	Since $b_p/a_p\ge1-1/p$ and $c_p/a_p=(p+1)/(p+2)\ge1-1/p$, we have $h(q)\ge IA_h\,\varphi(q)/q\gg_\eps q^{-\eps}$, where $A_h=\prod_pa_p>0$ (\cref{prop:poly}(0)). So \cref{prop:MT} gives $\MT(x;q)=h(q)\sqrt{xq}\,\bigl(1+O_\eps(x^{2\eps}(q/x)^{1/6})\bigr)$. The relative error is not small when $q\asymp x$. This is why the asymptotic formula of \cref{thm:main}(iii) requires $Y\le x^{1-\delta}$, whereas the error term in~(ii), which keeps $\MT$ unexpanded, has no such restriction. The numerical data in \cref{sec:numerics} suggest that, after summation over the moduli, the secondary term has relative size roughly proportional to $\sqrt{Y/x}$. That is consistent with, but sharper than, the proved bound.
   147	\end{remark}
\section{The variance for a single modulus}\label{sec:single}

\begin{proposition}[Single-modulus variance]\label{prop:single}
For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_7(\eps)$ such that for all real $x\ge2$ and all integers $1\le q\le x$:
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item $|V(x;q)-\MT(x;q)|\le c_7(\eps)\bigl(x^{5/3+\eps}/q+\sqrt x\bigr)$;
\item $|V(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}|\le c_7(\eps)\bigl(x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}+x^{5/3+\eps}/q+\sqrt x\bigr)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(i) By \cref{prop:identity}, which holds for all $x\ge1$ and $q\in\N$,
\[
V(x;q)-\MT(x;q)=2\sum_{1\le h\le x/q}D_x(hq)+\Bigl(Q(x)-\frac{6x}{\pi^2}\Bigr)-2x\sum_{l=1}^qg(q,l)E(x;q,l).
\]
For $1\le h\le x/q$ the integer $m=hq$ satisfies $1\le m\le x$. Since $x\ge2$, \cref{prop:pairs} applies to each of the at most $x/q$ terms. (This is the only place where $x\ge2$ rather than $x\ge1$ is needed.) It gives
\[
\Bigl|2\sum_{1\le h\le x/q}D_x(hq)\Bigr|\le2\cdot\frac xq\cdot c_3(\eps)x^{2/3+\eps}=2c_3(\eps)\frac{x^{5/3+\eps}}q .
\]
\Cref{prop:trivial}(i) gives $|Q(x)-6x/\pi^2|\le c_0\sqrt x$. \Cref{prop:trivial}(ii) gives
\[
\Bigl|2x\sum_lg(q,l)E(x;q,l)\Bigr|\le2c_0\frac{x^{3/2}}q\le2c_0\frac{x^{5/3+\eps}}q,
\]
since $x\ge1$. By the triangle inequality, (i) holds with $c_7(\eps)\ge2c_3(\eps)+2c_0$.

(ii) \Cref{prop:MT} gives $|\MT(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}|\le c_6(\eps)x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}$. Combining this with (i) by the triangle inequality proves (ii) with
\[
c_7(\eps)=\max\bigl\{2c_3(\eps)+2c_0,\ c_6(\eps)\bigr\},
\]
and (i) remains true with this larger constant.
\end{proof}

# Manuscript: sparse variance of squarefree numbers to polynomial moduli

Files:

* `main.tex`: main file; `sections/*.tex`: the sections and appendices;
  `references.bib`: bibliography.
* `generated/`: every table fragment (`tab_*.tex`), plot data file (`fig_*.dat`),
  the macros for numbers quoted in the text (`macros.tex`), and the re-run
  snapshot output (`snapshot_rerun_results.json`). All of these are written by
  `reproduce.py`.
* `reproduce.py`: regenerates everything in `generated/` and writes
  `reproduction.json` (list of artifacts, their sources, parameters, fits,
  constants and checks).
* `changes.md`: map from the manuscript to the archived run, with notation
  changes, merged arguments, corrections and additions.

## Reproduction

Requirements (no installation or network access is needed or performed):
Python 3 with numpy, scipy, mpmath and sympy; `clang++` with C++17 support;
about 5 GB of free memory; roughly 12–15 minutes on a current laptop. The
run that produced the shipped artifacts records its own timings in
`reproduction.json` (`snapshot_rerun.seconds` for the snapshot re-run,
`snapshot_rerun.total_seconds_of_reproduce_py` for the whole script).

From the workspace root (the directory containing `source/` and `manuscript/`):

```sh
python3 manuscript/reproduce.py
```

This

1. checks the SHA-256 of `source/numerics/snapshot/compute.py` and
   `counts.cpp` against `source/numerics/accepted.json`, copies both into the
   scratch directory `scratch/reproduce-work/`, and runs `compute.py` there
   unchanged. That script compiles `counts.cpp` with
   `clang++ -O3 -std=c++17`, re-runs its validations, recomputes all
   11 sizes x = 2.5e5 … 2.56e8 for the three polynomials, and redoes the
   fits. The archived executable `counts` is not used;
2. compares the regenerated `results.json` with the archived one (recorded in
   `reproduction.json` under `snapshot_rerun`);
3. computes C_f (Euler products over p ≤ 1e7 with a rigorous tail bound;
   interval endpoints rounded outwards; a 40-digit recomputation for
   p ≤ 1e5 as a check of floating-point rounding), Vaughan's c_2, the
   exact-shape sums `Σ f'(k) MT(x; f(k))` and `Σ F(k) h(f(k))`, symbolic
   checks, a self-test of the exact identity (Proposition 4.1), and, for each
   row at the largest x, the range of δ for which it lies in the range of
   Theorem 1.1(iii);
4. checks the qualitative statements made in Section 10 against the data
   (the script stops with an error if one fails) and writes
   `manuscript/generated/*` (including `macros.tex`, which holds every number
   quoted in the prose of Section 10) and `manuscript/reproduction.json`.

Options: `--work DIR` selects another scratch directory. The script refuses to
delete a non-empty directory that it did not create. `--reuse-work` reuses a
`results.json` already present in the scratch directory instead of re-running
the snapshot (for quick iterations only).

## Compilation

```sh
cd manuscript
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error -no-shell-escape main.tex
```

The build uses only standard TeX Live packages (amsmath/amsthm, thmtools,
mathtools, pgfplots, booktabs, enumitem, hyperref, cleveref, microtype) and
BibTeX with the `plainurl` style. No shell escape is needed. `reproduce.py`
must have been run first, because the text inputs `generated/macros.tex` and
the generated tables.

## Bibliography limitations

* All works cited are in the supplied corpus (`papers/`). No historical
  attribution is made for the pair-count estimate of Proposition 5.1, whose
  proof is self-contained; the only related remark (Section 5) quotes what
  BGPVW (1998, §1, p. 3) report about Evelyn and Linfoot, whose papers were
  not consulted and are not cited separately.
* Goldston–Vaughan (1997) and Vaughan (1998, I) are cited only for the
  attribution made by Brüdern–Wooley (2011, §1); their content was not used.
* The supplied Brüdern–Wooley PDF is a preprint without journal header
  (PDF creation date 2009). The venue (Quart. J. Math. 62 (2011), 289–305) is
  taken from `papers/INDEX.md`. For it and for
  Brüdern–Granville–Perelli–Vaughan–Wooley (1998), whose venue is also taken
  from `papers/INDEX.md`, no URL, DOI or arXiv identifier is given in the
  supplied material, and none could be verified without network access. The
  bibliography entries say so; no locator was invented.
* Montgomery–Vaughan (2007): Theorem 1.8/1.9, Theorem 1.12, (2.20) and
  Corollary 10.4 were checked in the supplied chapters. Appendix B (Euler–Maclaurin
  summation) is not in the supplied corpus; the manuscript proves the needed
  Euler–Maclaurin lemma directly.
* Earlier work on the squarefree variance (Orr, Warlimont, Croft) is mentioned
  only as quoted in Vaughan (2005) and is not cited separately.

338	## Reproduction
339	
340	Requirements (no installation or network access is needed or performed):
341	Python 3 with numpy, scipy, mpmath and sympy; `clang++` with C++17 support;
342	about 5 GB of free memory; roughly 12–15 minutes on a current laptop. The
343	run that produced the shipped artifacts records its own timings in
344	`reproduction.json` (`snapshot_rerun.seconds` for the snapshot re-run,
345	`snapshot_rerun.total_seconds_of_reproduce_py` for the whole script).
346	
347	From the workspace root (the directory containing `source/` and `manuscript/`):
348	
349	```sh
350	python3 manuscript/reproduce.py
351	```
352	
353	This
354	
355	1. checks the SHA-256 of `source/numerics/snapshot/compute.py` and
356	   `counts.cpp` against `source/numerics/accepted.json`, copies both into the
357	   scratch directory `scratch/reproduce-work/`, and runs `compute.py` there
358	   unchanged. That script compiles `counts.cpp` with
359	   `clang++ -O3 -std=c++17`, re-runs its validations, recomputes all
360	   11 sizes x = 2.5e5 … 2.56e8 for the three polynomials, and redoes the
361	   fits. The archived executable `counts` is not used;
362	2. compares the regenerated `results.json` with the archived one (recorded in
363	   `reproduction.json` under `snapshot_rerun`);
364	3. computes C_f (Euler products over p ≤ 1e7 with a rigorous tail bound;
365	   interval endpoints rounded outwards; a 40-digit recomputation for
366	   p ≤ 1e5 as a check of floating-point rounding), Vaughan's c_2, the
367	   exact-shape sums `Σ f'(k) MT(x; f(k))` and `Σ F(k) h(f(k))`, symbolic
368	   checks, a self-test of the exact identity (Proposition 4.1), and, for each
369	   row at the largest x, the range of δ for which it lies in the range of
370	   Theorem 1.1(iii);
371	4. checks the qualitative statements made in Section 10 against the data
372	   (the script stops with an error if one fails) and writes
373	   `manuscript/generated/*` (including `macros.tex`, which holds every number
374	   quoted in the prose of Section 10) and `manuscript/reproduction.json`.
375	
376	Options: `--work DIR` selects another scratch directory. The script refuses to
377	delete a non-empty directory that it did not create. `--reuse-work` reuses a
378	`results.json` already present in the scratch directory instead of re-running
379	the snapshot (for quick iterations only).
380

1	# Changes: from the archived run to the manuscript
     2	
     3	This file maps every result in `main.tex` to its source in the archived run
     4	(`source/`), records the two referee reports for each proposition, and lists
     5	every notation change, merged argument, correction and addition.
     6	
     7	Archive: `source/` (archive label `zt-neutral`, archive commit
     8	`ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba`); selected plan
     9	`simplest@claude-opus-5-5` (`source/plan.md`, `source/plan.json`).
    10	For every proposition PN, `source/props/PN/review-v1-0.json` is the review by
    11	`claude-opus-5-5` and `source/props/PN/review-v1-1.json` the review by
    12	`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`. Both reviewers passed all nine propositions in round 1
    13	(severities: none or cosmetic). The assembly/integration reports are
    14	`source/report/assembly-claude-opus-5-5.md`,
    15	`source/report/assembly-codex-gpt-6.1-sol.md`,
    16	`source/report/integration-*.json` and `source/report/integration.json`.
    17	
    18	The theorem is stated with exactly the strength, ranges, hypotheses and
    19	error terms of the plan's main theorem and of P9. The weight `f'(k)` and the
    20	class of `f` are unchanged. No proposition is used outside its stated range.
    21	No mathematical change was made beyond the local corrections listed in §4.
    22	They were identified by the run's referees, by the operator audit recorded in
    23	`source/interventions.md` (2026-11-03 10:21), or by the two referees of the
    24	first round of this write-up (`feedback/0.json`, `feedback/1.json`). None of
    25	them weakens a statement or changes the main theorem. A few auxiliary
    26	statements are stated slightly more strongly or more explicitly than in the
    27	archived statement files; each such case is taken from the archived proof or
    28	proved in full in the manuscript, and is listed in §4a. One auxiliary lemma
    29	(Lemma 2.6) received an extra hypothesis that holds in every application
    30	(§4, item 19).
    31	
    32	## 1. Map of results

    40	| Lemma 2.1 (tail bound) | P3 proof Step 0 `(*)`; also P1 proof (i), P4 proof (0), P5 proof (c) | P1, P3, P4, P5 |
    41	| Lemma 2.2 (residue-class count) | P1 proof (i) (`source/props/P1/proof.md` line 14); P3 proof Step 2 (line 33) | P1, P3 |

    64	## 2. Notation changes
    65	
    66	| Archived | Manuscript | Reason |
    67	|---|---|---|
    68	| `tau_p` (local factor of C_f; plan, P8, P9, reports) | `σ_p` | `τ(n)` is the divisor function (P3, P8) |
    69	| `c_0 = -4ζ(-1/2)` (P8 proof) | `I` (as in P5) | one name for one constant; `c_0` is now the absolute constant `3e^{2ζ(3/2)}` of P4 |
    70	| `A_p, B_p, D_p` (P8 proof) | `a_p, b_p, c_p` (as in the Sol assembly report) | `B` is the sawtooth function |

    72	| `c_1, c_2, c_3, c_5` (P8 shape constants), `C_1 = ∏_{p∈P_0} p^2`, truncation parameter `E` | `γ_1, …, γ_4`, `C_P`, `W` | avoid clashes with `c_1 = 60` (P5), `C_1` (Vaughan) and `E(x;q,l)` |
    73	| `δ_q` (P5) | `Δ_q` | `δ` is the range parameter of the theorem |
    74	| `f(t) = κ(t)1[(t,q)=1]`, `b = μ*f` (P5(c) proof) | `κ_q(t)`, `β = μ*κ_q` (the plan's name) | `f` is the polynomial |
    75	| `A(u)`, `E_1, …, E_5` (P5(b) proof) | `Φ(u)`, `R_1, …, R_5` | `A(m)`, `E(x;q,l)` |
    76	| `t = t_1 t_2 t_3`, `Z(t_2)` (P6 proof) | `t = t_0 t_1 t_2` (subscript = min(v_p(q), 2)), `Z_1` | mnemonic indexing |
    77	| local `h(p)` (P1 proof (iii)) | `u(p)` | `h(q)` is the main-term function |
    78	| `κ_r` (P4 proof) | `ν_r` | `κ(t)` |
    79	| `E_1, E_2, E_3` (P3 proof) | `𝓔_1, 𝓔_2, 𝓔_3` | `E(x;q,l)` |
    80	| generic `c(ε)` in P3, P5, P6, P7, P8 | `c_3(ε)`, `c_5(ε)`, `c_6(ε)`, `c_7(ε)`, `c_8(f), c_8(f,ε)` | to compose constants explicitly in §7 and §9 |
    81	| Vaughan's modulus bound `Q` in `V(x,Q)` (Vaughan 2005, quoted in §1.2) | `Y`, so `V(x,Y)` | `Q(x)` and `Q(x;q,l)` are the counting functions (write-up referee, round 1) |
    82	| actual ratio `ratio_actual` (snapshot) | `ϱ = f(y)/x` (§10.5) | distinguish from the target ratio `r` |
    83	
    84	## 3. Merged arguments
    85	
    86	* **Tail bound** `Σ_{a>w} a^{-2} ≤ 2/w`: proved four times in the archive (P1 (i),
    87	  P3 `(*)`, P4 (0), P5 (c)); stated once as Lemma 2.1 (P3's version, valid for all w > 0).
    88	* **Counting integers in a residue class** (`N/L + θ`): P1 (i) and P3 Step 2 →
    89	  Lemma 2.2.
    90	* **Coprime pairs of squarefree numbers**: the Euler product
    91	  `Σ μ(a)μ(b)/(ab)^2 = ∏_{p∤e}(1-2/p^2)` was derived twice by "local choices"
    92	  (P1 proof (iv), P3 proof Step 4). Lemma 2.5 states it once. Its proof groups
    93	  the pairs by n = ab, which turns the sum into the multiplicative series
    94	  `Σ μ(n)2^{ω(n)} n^{-2} 1[(n,e)=1]`. This is the same computation in a
    95	  shorter form.
    96	* **Squarefree numbers coprime to r**: P4 (i) (count of Q(x)) and P4 (ii) Step 3
    97	  (count of T_r) are the same estimate; Lemma 3.2 proves the general case, and
    98	  Proposition 3.3(i) is its case r = 1. The constant `3√x` of P4 (i) is unchanged.
    99	* **Facts on η, κ, A_0** scattered over P1, P2, P6 → Lemma 2.4.
   100	
   101	## 4. Corrections (all local; no weakening of any statement)
   102	
   103	1. **P1(iii), normalisation** (Sol review of P1, "other issues"; operator audit).
   104	   The proof states `q·μ(d) g_d/d²·1[g_d | n] = ∏_{p|d} h(p)`, with an
   105	   extraneous factor q. Corrected in Proposition 3.1(iii): `μ(d) g_d/d² 1[g_d|n]
   106	   = ∏_{p|d} u(p)` and `q g(q,n) = Σ_d μ²(d) ∏_{p|d} u(p)`.
   107	2. **P1(iii), convergence** (Sol review of P1, main objection, cosmetic;
   108	   operator audit). The claim `Σ_p |h(p)| ≤ Σ_p p^{-2}` is false for p | q
   109	   (e.g. q = n = 2). Corrected: `|u(p)| = p^{-2}` for p ∤ q, and `|u(p)| ≤ 1` for
   110	   the finitely many p | q, so the series converges absolutely.
   111	3. **P3 Step 3, constant** (Opus review of P3). The proof writes
   112	   `2·(π²/6)·Σ e^{-2}(2e/z) ≤ (4π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`; the left side equals
   113	   `(2π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`. The original inequality was true but overestimated by a factor 2. The manuscript uses
   114	   the correct value and the bound `7τ(m)/z` instead of `14τ(m)/z`. The final
   115	   constant `(3 + 9C(ε))` replaces `2(1+τ*) + 1 + 14τ*`. Statement unchanged.
   116	4. **P8 §3.4, endpoint k = 1** (Opus review of P8, cosmetic; operator audit;
   117	   flagged as "P8 endpoint clarification" in `interventions.md`). The proof
   118	   treats the closed first interval `[1, β]` as `(1-δ, β]`. That needs F to be defined and
   119	   monotone left of 1, which fails e.g. for f = 3t − 1. Corrected by stating
   120	   the counting lemma (Lemma 8.5) for arbitrary intervals (open, closed or
   121	   half-open). Its proof only uses that `k_1 − e` and `k_n + e` lie outside the
   122	   interval. The closed interval `[1, β]` is then covered directly, and the constant
   123	   `3(2d−1) ≤ 6d` in eq. (8.10) (source eq. (3.9)) is unchanged.
   124	5. **P8 §3.5, implicit error term** (Opus review of P8). The source writes
   125	   `O(Y^{3/2} y^{-1/2})` for the term `(2/3)(Y^{3/2} − f(1)^{3/2})·O(y^{-1/2})`
   126	   without saying where it comes from. The assembly display in §8.3 now shows
   127	   it. The short-sum bound keeps the factor `(1 + log W)` (P8 (3.6)) explicitly,
   128	   and it is absorbed by the choice `ε ≤ 1/8` (the source absorbs it into
   129	   `E^{2ε}`). The final bound is unchanged.
   130	6. **P8 §3.2(ii), constant dependence** (Opus review of P8). The bound
   131	   `(2d)^{ω(n)} ≤ C n^ε` has a constant depending on d; this is now stated
   132	   (`C(f, ε)`).
   133	7. **P2, wording** (Opus review of P2). The parenthetical after (3) ("finitely
   134	   many nonzero terms after the bracket is rewritten") is replaced by: the
   135	   bracket vanishes for `q m_t(q) > x` (twice an empty sum), and each of the
   136	   three series obtained by splitting it converges absolutely.
   137	8. **P4 (i), wording** (Opus review of P4). "Every squarefree-indicator
   138	   identity gives" → derived from `μ²(n) = Σ_{d²|n} μ(d)` (Lemma 3.2).
   139	9. **P5(b), small s** (Opus review of P5). The two quantities both lie in
   140	   `[0, Λ/4]`, so their difference is at most `Λ/4` (source: `Λ/2`). The constant
   141	   `c_1 = 60` is kept.
   142	10. **P9, real-variable hypothesis** (Opus review of P9). The step
   143	    `f(k) ≤ f(y)` for real y uses `f'(t) ≥ 1` for all real `t ≥ 1`. This is
   144	    now explicit in (1.1) and in §9. The convention `1 ≤ k ≤ y` (integers) is
   145	    explicit in (1.2). The constants `c(ε/3)`, `c(f, ε/3)` and their
   146	    combination are written out in §9.
   147	11. **P9 remark on δ < 1/9** (Opus review of P9). Non-emptiness of the range
   148	    holds for x > 1; stated so.
   149	12. **P7, role of x ≥ 2** (Opus review of P7). Noted in the proof of
   150	    Proposition 7.1 that x ≥ 2 is needed only for P3.
   151	13. **P3, n ≥ 1** (Opus review of P3). C_x(m) counts positive n; explicit in
   152	    eq. (4.1).
   153	14. **P1(iii), sign of n** (Opus review of P1). Stated for squarefree `n ∈ ℕ`,
   154	    the only case used.
   155	15. **P5, citation "MV Thm B.5"** (Opus review of P5: not found in the
   156	    supplied PDF). Appendix B of Montgomery–Vaughan is not in the supplied
   157	    corpus. Its §1.3 refers to "Theorem B.5" for Euler–Maclaurin summation.
   158	    The manuscript proves Lemma 2.6 directly and cites only MV §1.3 and
   159	    Theorem 1.12 for comparison.
   160	16. **Unused numerical notes in the proofs** (not reproduced):
   161	    * P2: the proof's check agreed only to ~1e-3 because of truncation (Opus
   162	      review); replaced by the exact self-test in `reproduce.py`
   163	      (`identity_selftest`, agreement 4.8e-10).
   164	    * P6: the tail estimate `A_0 x/(q·3000)` wrongly contains 1/q (Sol review),
   165	      and the difference 92 at (10^6, 1) is a truncation artefact (Opus review).
   166	    * P8: "ρ(p²) ≈ ρ(p)/p, exact for these squarefree f" is false for root
   167	      counts (should be ρ(p²) = ρ(p) for unramified p); Sol review and Sol
   168	      assembly report §5. Also flagged in the operator audit.
   169	    * P1, P5: numerical sanity checks are not reproduced; P5's constants were
   170	      checked by the referees.
   171	17. **Remark 1.2 (range of part (ii))**. The plan says statement (a)/(ii)
   172	    "remains meaningful up to f(y) ~ x". The manuscript states only what is
   173	    proved: the error term of (ii) is of smaller order than `x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}`
   174	    for `x^{7/9+δ} ≤ Y ≤ x`. No lower bound for `Σ f'(k) MT(x; f(k))` is
   175	    claimed.
   176	18. **References.** P8's "Hooley 1964 (background on rho only; not needed)" is
   177	    dropped because no statement from it is used. The plan named a 1949 paper
   178	    of Mirsky on pairs of squarefree numbers from memory. Earlier versions of
   179	    this write-up cited Mirsky, Bull. AMS 55 (1949), from
   180	    `bibliography-candidates.json`, without having consulted it. Following the
   181	    round-1 write-up review (`feedback/0.json`, issue 7), that unverifiable
   182	    historical attribution is dropped. Section 5 now quotes only what the
   183	    supplied BGPVW (1998, §1) says about the related additive problem (see §5).
   184	19. **Lemma 2.6 / P5 Lemma EM, the case b = ∞** (write-up referee
   185	    `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, round 1, `feedback/1.json` issue 1). P5 proof line 11
   186	    states the infinite-interval formula under `F, F' → 0`, `F'' ∈ L^1`. That is
   187	    not enough: `G(u) = cos(log u)/u` on `[1, ∞)` satisfies these conditions,
   188	    but its integral diverges. The manuscript adds the hypothesis that
   189	    `∫_a^∞ G` converges, proves the limit passage, and notes that every
   190	    application satisfies it: `G(u) = u^{-s}` with `Re s > 1` in Proposition
   191	    6.1(a) (P5 line 23), and `Φ(u) = Z/u² − Z²/u⁴` on `(T, ∞)` in Proposition
   192	    6.1(b) (P5 line 53). The argument of P5, and hence every statement, is
   193	    unaffected. This makes explicit a hypothesis that holds in every use; it is
   194	    not a repair of a gap in the argument.
   195	20. **Proposition 6.1(b), arithmetic of the final sum** (write-up referee
   196	    `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, round 1, issue 2). The round-1 manuscript wrote the
   197	    sum of the bounds for `R_1, …, R_5` as `< 56.1Λ`. It equals
   198	    `449/8 Λ = 56.125Λ`. This was an error introduced in the write-up: the
   199	    archived P5 proof (line 65) has the correct bound `< 57Λ`, with the
   200	    decimal approximation "56.1" written as a rounding. Corrected to
   201	    `= 449/8 Λ < 57Λ`. The constant `c_1 = 60` is unchanged.
   202	
   203	## 4a. Statements stated more explicitly or more strongly than the archived statement files
   204	
   205	Each item is either proved in the archived proof (with line reference) or
   206	proved in full in the manuscript. None is used to strengthen the main theorem.
   207	(Identified as unrecorded in the round-1 write-up review, `feedback/0.json`,
   208	issue 2.)
   209	
   210	* **Proposition 6.2 (P6), range.** `source/props/P6/statement.md` states the
   211	  bound for real `x ≥ 1` and integers `1 ≤ q ≤ x`. The manuscript states it
   212	  for all real `x > 0` and all `q ∈ ℕ`, adding "in particular for `x ≥ 1`,
   213	  `1 ≤ q ≤ x`". Source: P6 proof Step 2, line 50 ("No use was made of q ≤ x or
   214	  x ≥ 1 in this step; the error bound holds for all x > 0, q ≥ 1"), and the
   215	  Conclusion, line 71.
   216	* **Proposition 6.1(b) (P5(b)), explicit constant.** The statement file has
   217	  "an absolute constant c_1"; the manuscript states `c_1 = 60`. Source: P5
   218	  proof line 37 ("I show this with c_1 = 60").
   219	* **Proposition 3.3 (P4), explicit constant.** The statement file has "an
   220	  absolute constant c_0"; the manuscript states `c_0 = 3e^{2ζ(3/2)}`. Source: P4
   221	  proof line 68. The manuscript also notes, as in P4 proof line 17, that `q ≤ x`
   222	  is not used in (ii).
   223	* **Lemma 3.2 (P4 Step 3).** `|T_r(y) − ν_r y| ≤ 3·2^{ω(r)} √y` for all `y > 0` is
   224	  P4 proof estimate (3), lines 45–48. Its case `r = 1`, `|Q(y) − 6y/π²| ≤ 3√y`
   225	  for all `y > 0`, extends P4(i) (stated for `x ≥ 1`, line 13) to `0 < y < 1`.
   226	  That case is trivial: `Q(y) = 0` and `6y/π² < 3√y`. It is not used.
   227	* **Lemma 2.2, strict inequality.** P1 proof line 14 and P3 proof line 33 use
   228	  `N/L + θ` with `|θ| ≤ 1`. Lemma 2.2 states and proves `|θ| < 1`. Every use
   229	  needs only `|θ| ≤ 1`.
   230	* **Proposition 5.1 (P3), constant.** `(3 + 9C(ε))` instead of
   231	  `2(1+τ*) + 1 + 14τ*`; see §4 item 3.
   232	
   233	## 5. Material added after the run
   234	
   235	None of the following is used in a proof.
   236	
   237	* **Section 1 background**: Vaughan's theorem for the full variance (2005,
   238	  (1.12)–(1.16)), the earlier `x²𝓕(x/Y)` results it quotes, and the
   239	  Brüdern–Wooley theorem (2011, Theorem in §1), all read from the supplied PDFs.
   240	* **Section 5, first paragraph**: the remark that BGPVW (1998, §1) report an
   241	  elementary argument of Evelyn and Linfoot giving
   242	  `r_k(n) = S_k(n) n + O(n^{2/(k+1)+ε})` for sums of two k-free numbers (read
   243	  from the supplied PDF, p. 3). It is background only.
   244	* **Remark 1.3**: the identity `σ_p|_{ρ≡1} = C_{1,p}(1 − p^{-2})²` of local
   245	  factors. The run checked `C_t = c_2` numerically to 7–8 digits (plan;
   246	  Opus assembly report §3). The write-up verifies the identity symbolically
   247	  with sympy (`reproduce.py`, `symbolic_local_identity`).
   248	* **Section 10** is recomputed from scratch by `manuscript/reproduce.py`:
   249	  * re-run of the accepted snapshot code (unchanged; recompiled), with
   250	    an exact comparison against the archived `results.json` (identical);
   251	  * C_f for k²+1, k³+2, 2k+1 and the formal f = t, with a rigorous bound for
   252	    the omitted primes. This uses the tail argument of the Sol assembly report §6, eq. (21),
   253	    which rests on eq. (8.2), `|σ_p − 1| ≤ (3+2d)/p²`, from P8 §1. The value for 2k+1
   254	    (not compared by either integrator) is new here; the plan quotes 0.14261;
   255	  * new code for `Σ f'(k) MT(x; f(k))` and `Σ F(k) h(f(k))`. The Opus integrator
   256	    did a similar computation with its own code, which is not in the archive.
   257	    The write-up's code evaluates the infinite t-series without truncation (closed-form tails)
   258	    and is checked against the exact identity of Proposition 4.1;
   259	  * the sensitivity table of the snapshot's extrapolation (values from the

# Manuscript: sparse variance of squarefree numbers to polynomial moduli

Files:

* `main.tex`: main file; `sections/*.tex`: the sections and appendices;
  `references.bib`: bibliography.
* `generated/`: every table fragment (`tab_*.tex`), plot data file (`fig_*.dat`),
  the macros for numbers quoted in the text (`macros.tex`), and the re-run
  snapshot output (`snapshot_rerun_results.json`). All of these are written by
  `reproduce.py`.
* `reproduce.py`: regenerates everything in `generated/` and writes
  `reproduction.json` (list of artifacts, their sources, parameters, fits,
  constants and checks).
* `changes.md`: map from the manuscript to the archived run, with notation
  changes, merged arguments, corrections and additions.

## Reproduction

Requirements (no installation or network access is needed or performed):
Python 3 with numpy, scipy, mpmath and sympy; `clang++` with C++17 support;
about 5 GB of free memory; roughly 12–15 minutes on a current laptop. The
run that produced the shipped artifacts records its own timings in
`reproduction.json` (`snapshot_rerun.seconds` for the snapshot re-run,
`snapshot_rerun.total_seconds_of_reproduce_py` for the whole script).

From the workspace root (the directory containing `source/` and `manuscript/`):

```sh
python3 manuscript/reproduce.py
```

This

1. checks the SHA-256 of `source/numerics/snapshot/compute.py` and
   `counts.cpp` against `source/numerics/accepted.json`, copies both into the
   scratch directory `scratch/reproduce-work/`, and runs `compute.py` there
   unchanged. That script compiles `counts.cpp` with
   `clang++ -O3 -std=c++17`, re-runs its validations, recomputes all
   11 sizes x = 2.5e5 … 2.56e8 for the three polynomials, and redoes the
   fits. The archived executable `counts` is not used;
2. compares the regenerated `results.json` with the archived one (recorded in
   `reproduction.json` under `snapshot_rerun`);
3. computes C_f (Euler products over p ≤ 1e7 with a rigorous tail bound;
   interval endpoints rounded outwards; a 40-digit recomputation for
   p ≤ 1e5 as a check of floating-point rounding), Vaughan's c_2, the
   exact-shape sums `Σ f'(k) MT(x; f(k))` and `Σ F(k) h(f(k))`, symbolic
   checks, a self-test of the exact identity (Proposition 4.1), and, for each
   row at the largest x, the range of δ for which it lies in the range of
   Theorem 1.1(iii);
4. checks the qualitative statements made in Section 10 against the data
   (the script stops with an error if one fails) and writes
   `manuscript/generated/*` (including `macros.tex`, which holds every number
   quoted in the prose of Section 10) and `manuscript/reproduction.json`.

Options: `--work DIR` selects another scratch directory. The script refuses to
delete a non-empty directory that it did not create. `--reuse-work` reuses a
`results.json` already present in the scratch directory instead of re-running
the snapshot (for quick iterations only).

## Compilation

```sh
cd manuscript
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error -no-shell-escape main.tex
```

The build uses only standard TeX Live packages (amsmath/amsthm, thmtools,
mathtools, pgfplots, booktabs, enumitem, hyperref, cleveref, microtype) and
BibTeX with the `plainurl` style. No shell escape is needed. `reproduce.py`
must have been run first, because the text inputs `generated/macros.tex` and
the generated tables.

## Bibliography limitations

* All works cited are in the supplied corpus (`papers/`). No historical
  attribution is made for the pair-count estimate of Proposition 5.1, whose
  proof is self-contained; the only related remark (Section 5) quotes what
  BGPVW (1998, §1, p. 3) report about Evelyn and Linfoot, whose papers were
  not consulted and are not cited separately.
* Goldston–Vaughan (1997) and Vaughan (1998, I) are cited only for the
  attribution made by Brüdern–Wooley (2011, §1); their content was not used.
* The supplied Brüdern–Wooley PDF is a preprint without journal header
  (PDF creation date 2009). The venue (Quart. J. Math. 62 (2011), 289–305) is
  taken from `papers/INDEX.md`. For it and for
  Brüdern–Granville–Perelli–Vaughan–Wooley (1998), whose venue is also taken
  from `papers/INDEX.md`, no URL, DOI or arXiv identifier is given in the
  supplied material, and none could be verified without network access. The
  bibliography entries say so; no locator was invented.
* Montgomery–Vaughan (2007): Theorem 1.8/1.9, Theorem 1.12, (2.20) and
  Corollary 10.4 were checked in the supplied chapters. Appendix B (Euler–Maclaurin
  summation) is not in the supplied corpus; the manuscript proves the needed
  Euler–Maclaurin lemma directly.
* Earlier work on the squarefree variance (Orr, Warlimont, Croft) is mentioned
  only as quoted in Vaughan (2005) and is not cited separately.

2	"""Regenerate every number in the manuscript's numerical tables and plots.
3	
4	Invoke from the workspace root:
5

8	What it does (details in manuscript/README.md):
9	
10	1. Copies the accepted snapshot's ``compute.py`` and ``counts.cpp`` from
11	   ``source/numerics/snapshot`` into a scratch work directory (after checking
12	   their SHA-256 against ``source/numerics/accepted.json``) and runs
13	   ``compute.py`` there unchanged.  That script compiles ``counts.cpp`` with
14	   clang++, re-runs its validations, recomputes V_f(x, y) on the full grid
15	   x = 2.5e5, ..., 2.56e8, and redoes the empirical fits.  The archived
16	   executable is not used.
17	2. Compares the regenerated ``results.json`` with the archived one.
18	3. Computes, with code in this file, the quantities of the theorem that are
19	   not part of the snapshot: the constant C_f (Euler product over p <= 1e7,
20	   with a rigorous bound for the omitted primes), Vaughan's constant c_2,
21	   the sums  sum_k f'(k) MT(x; f(k))  and  sum_k F(k) h(f(k))  at selected rows,
22	   and a self-test of the exact identity of Proposition 4.1 (P2).
23	4. Writes LaTeX table fragments and PGFPlots data files to
24	   ``manuscript/generated/`` and the index ``manuscript/reproduction.json``.
25	
26	No value is copied from proof prose or from the archived results; the
27	archived ``results.json`` is read only for the agreement check in step 2.
28	"""
29	import argparse
30	import hashlib
31	import itertools
32	import json
33	import math
34	import pathlib
35	import shutil
36	import subprocess
37	import sys
38	import time
39	from decimal import Decimal, ROUND_CEILING, ROUND_FLOOR
40	
41	import numpy as np
42	import mpmath as mp
43	import sympy
44	
45	HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
46	WS = HERE.parent
47	SNAP = WS / 'source' / 'numerics' / 'snapshot'
48	ACCEPTED = WS / 'source' / 'numerics' / 'accepted.json'
49	GEN = HERE / 'generated'
50	DEFAULT_WORK = WS / 'scratch' / 'reproduce-work'
51	MARKER = '.reproduce-work'
52	
53	NAMES = ['k^2+1', 'k^3+2', '2k+1']
54	TEXNAME = {'k^2+1': '$k^2+1$', 'k^3+2': '$k^3+2$', '2k+1': '$2k+1$', 't': '$t$ (formal)'}
55	POLY = {'k^2+1': (lambda k: k * k + 1, lambda k: 2 * k, 2),
56	        'k^3+2': (lambda k: k ** 3 + 2, lambda k: 3 * k * k, 3),
57	        '2k+1': (lambda k: 2 * k + 1, lambda k: 2, 1),
58	        't': (lambda k: k, lambda k: 1, 1)}
59	RATIOS = [.01, .02, .05, .1, .2, .4, .7, 1.]
60	PRIME_CUTOFFS = [10 ** 3, 10 ** 4, 10 ** 5, 10 ** 6, 10 ** 7]
61	# Rows of the exact-shape comparison (Table 5).  The linear polynomial has
62	# about x/2 moduli, so it is restricted to the two smallest sizes.
63	SHAPE_XS = {'k^2+1': [1000000, 16000000, 256000000],
64	            'k^3+2': [1000000, 16000000, 256000000],
65	            '2k+1': [250000, 1000000]}
66	
67	mp.mp.dps = 80
68	I_CONST = -4 * mp.zeta(mp.mpf(-1) / 2)          # I = -4 zeta(-1/2)
69	SIX_PI2 = 6 / mp.pi ** 2
70	
71	
72	def sha256(path):
73	    return hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()
74	
75	
76	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
77	# 1. Snapshot re-run
78	# ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
79	
80	def run_snapshot(work, reuse):
81	    accepted = json.loads(ACCEPTED.read_text())['artifacts']
82	    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
83	        if sha256(SNAP / name) != accepted[name]:
84	            raise RuntimeError(f'{name} does not match the accepted snapshot hash')
85	    elapsed = None
86	    if not (reuse and (work / 'results.json').exists()):
87	        if work.exists():
88	            # Only ever delete a directory that this script created itself.
89	            if any(work.iterdir()) and not (work / MARKER).exists():
90	                raise RuntimeError(f'{work} is not empty and was not created by reproduce.py; '
91	                                   'choose another --work directory')
92	            shutil.rmtree(work)
93	        work.mkdir(parents=True)
94	        (work / MARKER).write_text('scratch directory of manuscript/reproduce.py; safe to delete\n')
95	        for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
96	            shutil.copy2(SNAP / name, work / name)
97	        t0 = time.monotonic()
98	        subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(work / 'compute.py')], cwd=work, check=True)
99	        elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
100	    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
101	        if sha256(work / name) != accepted[name]:
102	            raise RuntimeError(f'work copy of {name} differs from the snapshot')
103	    results = json.loads((work / 'results.json').read_text())
104	    return results, elapsed
105	
106	
107	def all_rows(res, name):
108	    p = res['polynomials'][name]
109	    return p['rows'] + p['diagnostic_rows']
110	
111	
112	def compare_with_archive(new):
113	    old = json.loads((SNAP / 'results.json').read_text())
114	    out = {}
115	    for name in NAMES:
116	        o = {(r['x'], r['ratio_target']): r for r in all_rows(old, name)}
117	        n = {(r['x'], r['ratio_target']): r for r in all_rows(new, name)}
118	        if set(o) != set(n):
119	            raise RuntimeError(f'row sets differ for {name}')
120	        exact = all(o[k]['sum_Q_squared_weighted'] == n[k]['sum_Q_squared_weighted']
121	                    and o[k]['y'] == n[k]['y'] for k in o)
122	        dv = max(abs(Decimal(o[k]['V_decimal']) / Decimal(n[k]['V_decimal']) - 1) for k in o)
123	        po, pn = old['polynomials'][name], new['polynomials'][name]
124	        ce_o, ce_n = po['constant_extrapolated'], pn['constant_extrapolated']
125	        out[name] = dict(rows=len(o), integer_counts_identical=exact,
126	                         max_relative_difference_V=float(dv),
127	                         extrapolated_constant_difference=abs(ce_o['value'] - ce_n['value']),
128	                         envelope_difference=abs(ce_o['uncertainty'] - ce_n['uncertainty']),
129	                         fixed_ratio_slope_difference=abs(po['fit_fixed_ratio']['alpha_plus_beta']
130	                                                          - pn['fit_fixed_ratio']['alpha_plus_beta']))

def sha256(path):
    return hashlib.sha256(pathlib.Path(path).read_bytes()).hexdigest()

def run_snapshot(work, reuse):
    accepted = json.loads(ACCEPTED.read_text())['artifacts']
    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
        if sha256(SNAP / name) != accepted[name]:
            raise RuntimeError(f'{name} does not match the accepted snapshot hash')
    elapsed = None
    if not (reuse and (work / 'results.json').exists()):
        if work.exists():
            # Only ever delete a directory that this script created itself.
            if any(work.iterdir()) and not (work / MARKER).exists():
                raise RuntimeError(f'{work} is not empty and was not created by reproduce.py; '
                                   'choose another --work directory')
            shutil.rmtree(work)
        work.mkdir(parents=True)
        (work / MARKER).write_text('scratch directory of manuscript/reproduce.py; safe to delete\n')
        for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
            shutil.copy2(SNAP / name, work / name)
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        subprocess.run([sys.executable, str(work / 'compute.py')], cwd=work, check=True)
        elapsed = time.monotonic() - t0
    for name in ['compute.py', 'counts.cpp']:
        if sha256(work / name) != accepted[name]:
            raise RuntimeError(f'work copy of {name} differs from the snapshot')
    results = json.loads((work / 'results.json').read_text())
    return results, elapsed

        raise RuntimeError(f'a statement of Section 10 is not supported by the data: {claims}')
    pct = lambda v: f'{100 * v:+.2f}'

    # Macros for numbers quoted in the text
    macros = {
        'CfQuadCert': certified_digits(consts['k^2+1']['lower'], consts['k^2+1']['upper']),
        'CfCubicCert': certified_digits(consts['k^3+2']['lower'], consts['k^3+2']['upper']),

        'RelLin': pct(fitsum['2k+1']['relative_difference']),

def write_reproduction(repro, total):
    repro['snapshot_rerun']['total_seconds_of_reproduce_py'] = total
    (HERE / 'reproduction.json').write_text(json.dumps(repro, indent=2) + '\n')


def main():
    ap = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__, formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter)
    ap.add_argument('--work', type=pathlib.Path, default=DEFAULT_WORK,
                    help='scratch directory for the snapshot re-run (default: scratch/reproduce-work)')
    ap.add_argument('--reuse-work', action='store_true',
                    help='reuse results.json already present in the work directory instead of re-running the snapshot')
    args = ap.parse_args()
    t0 = time.monotonic()
    results, elapsed = run_snapshot(args.work.resolve(), args.reuse_work)
    print(f'snapshot results ready ({elapsed if elapsed is not None else "reused"})', flush=True)
    compare = compare_with_archive(results)
    print('comparison with archived results:', json.dumps(compare), flush=True)
    P = primes_upto(PRIME_CUTOFFS[-1])
    rho_checked = {name: rho_bruteforce_check(name) for name in NAMES + ['t']}
    consts = {name: euler_constant(name, P) for name in NAMES + ['t']}
    c2 = vaughan_c2(P)
    symb = symbolic_local_identity()
    xmax = max(max(v) for v in SHAPE_XS.values())
    ar = Arithmetic(math.isqrt(xmax) + 2)
    selftest = identity_selftest(ar)
    print(f'identity self-test: max relative discrepancy {selftest:.2e}', flush=True)
    if selftest > 1e-8:
        raise RuntimeError('identity self-test failed')
    shape = shape_rows(results, ar)
    floatcheck = {}
    for name in NAMES + ['t']:
        exact = euler_float_check(name)
        floatcheck[name] = float(abs(consts[name]['partial'][10 ** 5] / exact - 1))
    print('float check of the Euler products:', floatcheck, flush=True)
    elig = {name: eligibility(results, name) for name in NAMES}
    repro = make_outputs(results, compare, consts, c2, shape, selftest, symb, rho_checked, elapsed, floatcheck, elig)
    write_reproduction(repro, time.monotonic() - t0)
    print(f'done in {time.monotonic() - t0:.1f}s; wrote {HERE / "reproduction.json"}', flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

\section{Sawtooth sums and the main term for one modulus}\label{sec:sawtooth}

\subsection{Sawtooth sums}

The function $B(u)=\fr u(1-\fr u)$ is continuous, $1$-periodic, takes values in $[0,\frac14]$, and satisfies $B(u)=u-u^2$ for $0\le u\le1$. The sums we need are $\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)$ and weighted versions of them. Their size $\asymp\sqrt Z$ has two sources: the terms with $s>\sqrt Z$, where $B(Z/s^2)=Z/s^2-Z^2/s^4$, and the terms with $s\le\sqrt Z$, where $B$ oscillates. The natural approximation is the integral $\int_0^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du=I\sqrt Z$ (substitute $u=\sqrt Z\,w$). For $q\in\N$ put
\[
\kappa_q(t)=\kappa(t)\one[(t,q)=1],\qquad \Delta_q=\prod_p\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\one[p\nmid q]\frac{p}{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
For $p\nmid q$ the factor of $\Delta_q$ is $(p-1)^2(p+2)/(p(p^2-2))=1+O(p^{-2})$; there are finitely many other factors, so the product converges absolutely.

\begin{proposition}[Sawtooth sums]\label{prop:sawtooth}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $I=\int_0^\infty B(u^{-2})\,du=\frac12\int_0^\infty B(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=-4\zeta(-\tfrac12)$.
\item For every real $Z>0$, $\bigl|\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z\bigr|\le c_1Z^{1/3}$ with $c_1=60$.
\item For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_5(\eps)$ such that for all $q\in\N$ and real $Z>0$,
\[
\Bigl|\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-\Delta_q\,I\sqrt Z\Bigr|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^\eps Z^{1/3}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) The substitution $v=u^{-2}$ gives the second expression. The integral converges, because $B(v)\le v$ near $0$ and $B(v)\le\frac14$. Since $B$ is continuous and piecewise $C^1$ with $B'(v)=1-2\fr v$, integration by parts on $[0,X]$ gives
\[
\int_0^XB(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=\bigl[-2B(v)v^{-1/2}\bigr]_0^X+2\int_0^XB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv .
\]
The boundary term tends to $0$, because $B(v)v^{-1/2}\le v^{1/2}$ near $0$ and $B(X)X^{-1/2}\le\frac14X^{-1/2}$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=2\lim_{N\to\infty}\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv$ along integers $N$. On $(n,n+1)$ we have $B'(n^+)=1$, $B'((n+1)^-)=-1$ and $B''=-2$, so integrating by parts with the antiderivative $2v^{1/2}$ of $v^{-1/2}$,
\[
\int_n^{n+1}B'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-2(n+1)^{1/2}-2n^{1/2}+4\int_n^{n+1}v^{1/2}\,dv,
\]
and summing over $0\le n<N$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Bprime}
\int_0^NB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-4\sum_{m=1}^Nm^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+\tfrac83N^{3/2}.
\end{equation}
Now apply \cref{lem:EM} on $(N,\infty)$ to $G(u)=u^{-s}$ with $\Re s>1$, using $\psi(N)=-\frac12$ and $\psi_2(N)=\frac1{12}$:
\[
\sum_{n>N}n^{-s}=\frac{N^{1-s}}{s-1}-\frac{N^{-s}}2+\frac s{12}N^{-s-1}-s(s+1)\int_N^\infty\psi_2(u)u^{-s-2}\,du .
\]
The right-hand side is analytic in $\Re s>-1$, $s\ne1$, because the integral converges locally uniformly there. By uniqueness of analytic continuation, $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le N}n^{-s}$ plus the right-hand side in that region. At $s=-\frac12$ we have $s(s+1)=-\frac14$ and $|\int_N^\infty\psi_2u^{-3/2}\,du|\le\frac16N^{-1/2}$, so
\[
\sum_{m\le N}m^{1/2}=\zeta(-\tfrac12)+\tfrac23N^{3/2}+\tfrac12N^{1/2}+O(N^{-1/2}).
\]
Inserting this into~\eqref{eq:Bprime} shows that $\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv\to-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=-8\zeta(-\frac12)$ and $I=-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. By the functional equation~\cite[Corollary~10.4]{MV2007} at $s=-\frac12$, $\zeta(-\frac12)=2^{-1/2}\pi^{-3/2}\Gamma(\frac32)\sin(-\frac\pi4)\zeta(\frac32)=-\zeta(\frac32)/(4\pi)$. So $I=\zeta(3/2)/\pi>0$, the value stated in~\eqref{eq:I}.

(b) \emph{The case $Z<1$.} Here $0\le B(Z/s^2)\le Z/s^2$, so $0\le\sum_sB(Z/s^2)\le\zeta(2)Z<2Z^{1/3}$. Also $0<I\sqrt Z<Z^{1/3}$, since $I<1$. The difference of two numbers in $[0,2Z^{1/3}]$ is at most $2Z^{1/3}$.

\emph{The case $Z\ge1$.} Put $\Lambda=Z^{1/3}\ge1$ and $T=\lfloor\Lambda\rfloor\ge1$. Then $\Lambda/2<T\le\Lambda$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:b1}
\frac Z{T^3}<8,\qquad K_0:=\frac Z{T^2}<4\Lambda,\qquad \frac{Z^2}{T^5}<32\Lambda .
\end{equation}
\emph{Small $s$.} Both $\sum_{s\le T}B(Z/s^2)$ and $\int_0^TB(Z/u^2)\,du$ lie in $[0,T/4]\subset[0,\Lambda/4]$, so their difference is at most $\Lambda/4$. It therefore suffices to show
\begin{equation}\label{eq:b2}
\Bigl|\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)-\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du\Bigr|\le57\Lambda ,
\end{equation}
which gives the claim with $57+\frac14<60$.

\emph{A decomposition of $B$.} For real $w\ge0$ with $j=\lfloor w\rfloor$ we have $B(w)=(w-j)(1-w+j)=w-w^2+2jw-j-j^2$, and $\sum_{k=1}^j2(w-k)=2jw-j^2-j$. Hence
\[
B(w)=w-w^2+2\sum_{k\ge1}(w-k)_+,\qquad(v)_+=\max(v,0).
\]
Put $\Phi(u)=Z/u^2-Z^2/u^4$ and $G_k(u)=(Z/u^2-k)_+$, so that $B(Z/u^2)=\Phi(u)+2\sum_{k\ge1}G_k(u)$. For $u\ge T$ only the $k<K_0$ contribute, and there are fewer than $K_0<4\Lambda$ of them. For such $k$, $G_k(u)=Z/u^2-k$ on $[T,R_k]$ with $R_k=\sqrt{Z/k}>T$, and $G_k=0$ on $[R_k,\infty)$.

\emph{Euler--Maclaurin.} Apply \cref{lem:EM} to $\Phi$ on $(T,\infty)$, and to $Z/u^2-k$ on $(T,R_k]$ for each $k<K_0$. Use $\psi(T)=-\frac12$, $\psi_2(T)=\frac1{12}$ and $G_k(R_k)=0$, and add. Since $\int_T^\infty\Phi+2\sum_k\int_T^{R_k}G_k=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du$ (all integrals converge absolutely), this gives
\[
\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du+R_1+R_2+R_3+R_4+R_5,
\]
where, writing $G_k'$ and $G_k''$ for the derivatives of $Z/u^2-k$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $R_1=\psi(T)\bigl[\Phi(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k(T)\bigr]=\psi(T)B(Z/T^2)$. The individual terms here have size about $Z^2/T^4\asymp Z^{2/3}$, but their sum is $B(Z/T^2)\le\frac14$. So $|R_1|\le\frac18$. This is the one place where cancellation is essential.
\item $R_2=-\frac1{12}\bigl[\Phi'(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k'(T)\bigr]$, with $\Phi'(T)=-2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5$ and $G_k'(T)=-2Z/T^3$. By~\eqref{eq:b1}, $|\Phi'(T)|<16+128\Lambda$ and $|2\sum_kG_k'(T)|\le4K_0Z/T^3<128\Lambda$. So $|R_2|\le\frac1{12}(16+256\Lambda)\le\frac{272}{12}\Lambda$.
\item $R_3=-\int_T^\infty\psi_2\Phi''\,du$ with $\Phi''=6Z/u^4-20Z^2/u^6$. So $|R_3|\le\frac1{12}(2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5)<\frac1{12}(16+128\Lambda)\le12\Lambda$.
\item $R_4=-2\sum_{k<K_0}\int_T^{R_k}\psi_2G_k''\,du$ with $G_k''=6Z/u^4$ and $\int_T^\infty6Zu^{-4}\,du=2Z/T^3<16$. So $|R_4|\le\frac2{12}K_0\cdot16<\frac{32}3\Lambda$.
\item $R_5=2\sum_{k<K_0}\psi_2(R_k)G_k'(R_k)$ with $G_k'(R_k)=-2Z/R_k^3=-2k^{3/2}/\sqrt Z$. Since $k<4\Lambda$, $\sum_{k<K_0}k^{3/2}<4\Lambda\cdot8\Lambda^{3/2}$, and with $\sqrt Z=\Lambda^{3/2}$ we get $|R_5|\le\frac2{12}\cdot2\cdot32\Lambda=\frac{32}3\Lambda$. These are the kinks of the $G_k$ at the points $R_k$. Summing over the $K_0\asymp Z^{1/3}$ values of $k$ is what produces the exponent $\frac13$.
\end{itemize}
Using $\Lambda\ge1$, the total is at most $(\frac18+\frac{272}{12}+12+\frac{32}3+\frac{32}3)\Lambda=\frac{449}8\Lambda<57\Lambda$, which proves~\eqref{eq:b2}.

(c) Fix $q$. The function $\kappa_q$ is multiplicative with $\kappa_q(p)=p^2/(p^2-2)$ for $p\nmid q$, $\kappa_q(p)=0$ for $p\mid q$ and $\kappa_q(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$. Let $\beta=\mu*\kappa_q$, so that $\kappa_q=1*\beta$. Then $\beta$ is multiplicative, with $\beta(p^j)=\kappa_q(p^j)-\kappa_q(p^{j-1})$:
\begin{itemize}
\item for $p\mid q$: $\beta(p)=-1$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$;
\item for $p\nmid q$: $\beta(p)=\frac2{p^2-2}$, $\beta(p^2)=-\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge3$.
\end{itemize}
\emph{Absolute convergence.} For $p\nmid q$, $\sum_j|\beta(p^j)|p^{-2j/3}\le\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}$, because $p^2/(p^2-2)\le2$. Hence
\[
\Sigma_{2/3}:=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{|\beta(n)|}{n^{2/3}}\le\prod_{p\mid q}\bigl(1+p^{-2/3}\bigr)\prod_p\Bigl(1+\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}\Bigr)\le C_\beta\,2^{\omega(q)}\le C_\beta C(\eps)q^\eps,
\]
with an absolute constant $C_\beta$, by \cref{lem:divisor}. Similarly $\sum_n|\beta(n)|/n<\infty$ for each fixed $q$.

\emph{Rearrangement.} For $W>0$, $\sum_mB(W/m^2)\le\sum_m\min(\frac14,W/m^2)\le3\sqrt W$. Indeed, for $W<1$ the sum is at most $\zeta(2)W\le2\sqrt W$, and for $W\ge1$ it is at most $\frac14\sqrt W+W\cdot2/\sqrt W$ by \cref{lem:tail}. Hence $\sum_{n,m}|\beta(n)|B(Z/(nm)^2)\le3\sqrt Z\sum_n|\beta(n)|/n<\infty$, and we may rearrange:
\[
\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)=\sum_{n,m\ge1}\beta(n)B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr)=\sum_{n\ge1}\beta(n)\sum_{m\ge1}B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr).
\]
\emph{Main term.} Part (b) holds for every positive argument. Applying it with $Z/n^2$ in place of $Z$, and using $I\sqrt{Z/n^2}=I\sqrt Z/n$,
\[
\Bigl|\sum_t\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-I\sqrt Z\sum_n\frac{\beta(n)}n\Bigr|\le c_1\sum_n|\beta(n)|\Bigl(\frac Z{n^2}\Bigr)^{1/3}=c_1\Sigma_{2/3}Z^{1/3}.
\]
\emph{The constant.} By~\eqref{eq:euler}, $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\prod_p\bigl(1+\beta(p)/p+\beta(p^2)/p^2\bigr)$. For $p\mid q$ the factor is $1-1/p$. For $p\nmid q$ it is
\[
1+\frac2{p(p^2-2)}-\frac1{p^2-2}=\frac{p^3-3p+2}{p(p^2-2)}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p(p^2-2)}=\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\frac p{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
Hence $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\Delta_q$, and (c) holds with $c_5(\eps)=c_1C_\beta C(\eps)$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The main term for one modulus}

\begin{proposition}[Asymptotics of $\MT$]\label{prop:MT}
For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_6(\eps)$ such that for all real $x>0$ and all $q\in\N$,
\[
\bigl|\MT(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}\bigr|\le c_6(\eps)\,x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps},
\]
with $h$ as in~\eqref{eq:h}. In particular this holds for $x\ge1$ and $1\le q\le x$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Factorising $t$.} Fix $q$. Every squarefree $t$ factors uniquely as $t=t_0t_1t_2$, where $t_0$ is composed of primes $p\nmid q$, $t_1$ of primes $p\,\|\,q$, and $t_2$ of primes $p$ with $p^2\mid q$. Conversely, every such triple of squarefree numbers gives a squarefree $t$. Let $\mathcal S_1$ and $\mathcal S_2$ be the finite sets of admissible $t_1$ and $t_2$ (all of them divide $q$). For squarefree $t$, $\gcd(t^2,q)=\prod_{p\mid t}p^{\min(2,v_p(q))}=t_1t_2^2$, so
\[
m_t(q)=t_0^2t_1,\qquad\frac x{q\,m_t(q)}=\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\quad\text{with}\quad Z_1=\frac{x}{q\,t_1},\qquad \eta(t)m_t(q)=\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\kappa(t_0).
\]
By the absolute convergence in \cref{lem:eta} we may regroup:
\[
\MT(x;q)=A_0\,q\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\Sigma(t_1),\qquad\Sigma(t_1)=\sum_{t_0\ge1}\kappa_q(t_0)B\Bigl(\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\Bigr).
\]
\emph{Applying \cref{prop:sawtooth}(c).} With $Z=Z_1>0$ we get $\Sigma(t_1)=\Delta_qI\sqrt{Z_1}+\theta\,c_5(\eps)q^\eps Z_1^{1/3}$. Since $t_1\sqrt{Z_1}=\sqrt{x/q}\,t_1^{1/2}$ and $t_1Z_1^{1/3}=(x/q)^{1/3}t_1^{2/3}$,
\[
\MT(x;q)=A_0\Delta_qI\sqrt{xq}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)+R,
\]
\[
|R|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^{1+\eps}\Bigl(\frac xq\Bigr)^{1/3}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2),
\]
where we used $A_0\le1$. By~\eqref{eq:eta-bound}, $\sum_{t_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-4/3})$ and $\sum_{t_2}\eta(t_2)\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-2})$, both absolute constants. So $|R|\le c_6(\eps)x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}$.

\emph{The constant is $h(q)$.} The two finite sums are Euler products over the primes dividing $q$:
\[
\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}=\prod_{p\|q}\Bigl(1+\frac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr),\qquad\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)=\prod_{p^2\mid q}\Bigl(1+\frac1{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
Multiplying the absolutely convergent products $A_0$ and $\Delta_q$ factor by factor, the local factor at $p$ of the main coefficient is
\begin{align*}
p\nmid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac p{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2+p-2)}{p^3}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p^3}=a_p,\\
p\,\|\,q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-2+\sqrt p)}{p^3}=b_p,\\
p^2\mid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac1{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-1)}{p^3}=c_p .
\end{align*}
Together with the factor $I$, this is exactly $h(q)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Since $b_p/a_p\ge1-1/p$ and $c_p/a_p=(p+1)/(p+2)\ge1-1/p$, we have $h(q)\ge IA_h\,\varphi(q)/q\gg_\eps q^{-\eps}$, where $A_h=\prod_pa_p>0$ (\cref{prop:poly}(0)). So \cref{prop:MT} gives $\MT(x;q)=h(q)\sqrt{xq}\,\bigl(1+O_\eps(x^{2\eps}(q/x)^{1/6})\bigr)$. The relative error is not small when $q\asymp x$. This is why the asymptotic formula of \cref{thm:main}(iii) requires $Y\le x^{1-\delta}$, whereas the error term in~(ii), which keeps $\MT$ unexpanded, has no such restriction. The numerical data in \cref{sec:numerics} suggest that, after summation over the moduli, the secondary term has relative size roughly proportional to $\sqrt{Y/x}$. That is consistent with, but sharper than, the proved bound.
\end{remark}
