\section{Sawtooth sums and the main term for one modulus}\label{sec:sawtooth}

\subsection{Sawtooth sums}

The function $B(u)=\fr u(1-\fr u)$ is continuous, $1$-periodic, takes values in $[0,\frac14]$, and satisfies $B(u)=u-u^2$ for $0\le u\le1$. The sums we need are $\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)$ and weighted versions of them. Their size $\asymp\sqrt Z$ has two sources: the terms with $s>\sqrt Z$, where $B(Z/s^2)=Z/s^2-Z^2/s^4$, and the terms with $s\le\sqrt Z$, where $B$ oscillates. The natural approximation is the integral $\int_0^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du=I\sqrt Z$ (substitute $u=\sqrt Z\,w$). For $q\in\N$ put
\[
\kappa_q(t)=\kappa(t)\one[(t,q)=1],\qquad \Delta_q=\prod_p\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\one[p\nmid q]\frac{p}{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
For $p\nmid q$ the factor of $\Delta_q$ is $(p-1)^2(p+2)/(p(p^2-2))=1+O(p^{-2})$; there are finitely many other factors, so the product converges absolutely.

\begin{proposition}[Sawtooth sums]\label{prop:sawtooth}
\leavevmode
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\alph*)}]
\item $I=\int_0^\infty B(u^{-2})\,du=\frac12\int_0^\infty B(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=-4\zeta(-\tfrac12)$.
\item For every real $Z>0$, $\bigl|\sum_{s\ge1}B(Z/s^2)-I\sqrt Z\bigr|\le c_1Z^{1/3}$ with $c_1=60$.
\item For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_5(\eps)$ such that for all $q\in\N$ and real $Z>0$,
\[
\Bigl|\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-\Delta_q\,I\sqrt Z\Bigr|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^\eps Z^{1/3}.
\]
\end{enumerate}
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
(a) The substitution $v=u^{-2}$ gives the second expression. The integral converges, because $B(v)\le v$ near $0$ and $B(v)\le\frac14$. Since $B$ is continuous and piecewise $C^1$ with $B'(v)=1-2\fr v$, integration by parts on $[0,X]$ gives
\[
\int_0^XB(v)v^{-3/2}\,dv=\bigl[-2B(v)v^{-1/2}\bigr]_0^X+2\int_0^XB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv .
\]
The boundary term tends to $0$, because $B(v)v^{-1/2}\le v^{1/2}$ near $0$ and $B(X)X^{-1/2}\le\frac14X^{-1/2}$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=2\lim_{N\to\infty}\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv$ along integers $N$. On $(n,n+1)$ we have $B'(n^+)=1$, $B'((n+1)^-)=-1$ and $B''=-2$, so integrating by parts with the antiderivative $2v^{1/2}$ of $v^{-1/2}$,
\[
\int_n^{n+1}B'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-2(n+1)^{1/2}-2n^{1/2}+4\int_n^{n+1}v^{1/2}\,dv,
\]
and summing over $0\le n<N$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:Bprime}
\int_0^NB'(v)v^{-1/2}\,dv=-4\sum_{m=1}^Nm^{1/2}+2N^{1/2}+\tfrac83N^{3/2}.
\end{equation}
Now apply \cref{lem:EM} on $(N,\infty)$ to $G(u)=u^{-s}$ with $\Re s>1$, using $\psi(N)=-\frac12$ and $\psi_2(N)=\frac1{12}$:
\[
\sum_{n>N}n^{-s}=\frac{N^{1-s}}{s-1}-\frac{N^{-s}}2+\frac s{12}N^{-s-1}-s(s+1)\int_N^\infty\psi_2(u)u^{-s-2}\,du .
\]
The right-hand side is analytic in $\Re s>-1$, $s\ne1$, because the integral converges locally uniformly there. By uniqueness of analytic continuation, $\zeta(s)=\sum_{n\le N}n^{-s}$ plus the right-hand side in that region. At $s=-\frac12$ we have $s(s+1)=-\frac14$ and $|\int_N^\infty\psi_2u^{-3/2}\,du|\le\frac16N^{-1/2}$, so
\[
\sum_{m\le N}m^{1/2}=\zeta(-\tfrac12)+\tfrac23N^{3/2}+\tfrac12N^{1/2}+O(N^{-1/2}).
\]
Inserting this into~\eqref{eq:Bprime} shows that $\int_0^NB'v^{-1/2}\,dv\to-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. Hence $\int_0^\infty Bv^{-3/2}\,dv=-8\zeta(-\frac12)$ and $I=-4\zeta(-\frac12)$. By the functional equation~\cite[Corollary~10.4]{MV2007} at $s=-\frac12$, $\zeta(-\frac12)=2^{-1/2}\pi^{-3/2}\Gamma(\frac32)\sin(-\frac\pi4)\zeta(\frac32)=-\zeta(\frac32)/(4\pi)$. So $I=\zeta(3/2)/\pi>0$, the value stated in~\eqref{eq:I}.

(b) \emph{The case $Z<1$.} Here $0\le B(Z/s^2)\le Z/s^2$, so $0\le\sum_sB(Z/s^2)\le\zeta(2)Z<2Z^{1/3}$. Also $0<I\sqrt Z<Z^{1/3}$, since $I<1$. The difference of two numbers in $[0,2Z^{1/3}]$ is at most $2Z^{1/3}$.

\emph{The case $Z\ge1$.} Put $\Lambda=Z^{1/3}\ge1$ and $T=\lfloor\Lambda\rfloor\ge1$. Then $\Lambda/2<T\le\Lambda$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:b1}
\frac Z{T^3}<8,\qquad K_0:=\frac Z{T^2}<4\Lambda,\qquad \frac{Z^2}{T^5}<32\Lambda .
\end{equation}
\emph{Small $s$.} Both $\sum_{s\le T}B(Z/s^2)$ and $\int_0^TB(Z/u^2)\,du$ lie in $[0,T/4]\subset[0,\Lambda/4]$, so their difference is at most $\Lambda/4$. It therefore suffices to show
\begin{equation}\label{eq:b2}
\Bigl|\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)-\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du\Bigr|\le57\Lambda ,
\end{equation}
which gives the claim with $57+\frac14<60$.

\emph{A decomposition of $B$.} For real $w\ge0$ with $j=\lfloor w\rfloor$ we have $B(w)=(w-j)(1-w+j)=w-w^2+2jw-j-j^2$, and $\sum_{k=1}^j2(w-k)=2jw-j^2-j$. Hence
\[
B(w)=w-w^2+2\sum_{k\ge1}(w-k)_+,\qquad(v)_+=\max(v,0).
\]
Put $\Phi(u)=Z/u^2-Z^2/u^4$ and $G_k(u)=(Z/u^2-k)_+$, so that $B(Z/u^2)=\Phi(u)+2\sum_{k\ge1}G_k(u)$. For $u\ge T$ only the $k<K_0$ contribute, and there are fewer than $K_0<4\Lambda$ of them. For such $k$, $G_k(u)=Z/u^2-k$ on $[T,R_k]$ with $R_k=\sqrt{Z/k}>T$, and $G_k=0$ on $[R_k,\infty)$.

\emph{Euler--Maclaurin.} Apply \cref{lem:EM} to $\Phi$ on $(T,\infty)$, and to $Z/u^2-k$ on $(T,R_k]$ for each $k<K_0$. Use $\psi(T)=-\frac12$, $\psi_2(T)=\frac1{12}$ and $G_k(R_k)=0$, and add. Since $\int_T^\infty\Phi+2\sum_k\int_T^{R_k}G_k=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du$ (all integrals converge absolutely), this gives
\[
\sum_{s>T}B(Z/s^2)=\int_T^\infty B(Z/u^2)\,du+R_1+R_2+R_3+R_4+R_5,
\]
where, writing $G_k'$ and $G_k''$ for the derivatives of $Z/u^2-k$:
\begin{itemize}
\item $R_1=\psi(T)\bigl[\Phi(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k(T)\bigr]=\psi(T)B(Z/T^2)$. The individual terms here have size about $Z^2/T^4\asymp Z^{2/3}$, but their sum is $B(Z/T^2)\le\frac14$. So $|R_1|\le\frac18$. This is the one place where cancellation is essential.
\item $R_2=-\frac1{12}\bigl[\Phi'(T)+2\sum_{k<K_0}G_k'(T)\bigr]$, with $\Phi'(T)=-2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5$ and $G_k'(T)=-2Z/T^3$. By~\eqref{eq:b1}, $|\Phi'(T)|<16+128\Lambda$ and $|2\sum_kG_k'(T)|\le4K_0Z/T^3<128\Lambda$. So $|R_2|\le\frac1{12}(16+256\Lambda)\le\frac{272}{12}\Lambda$.
\item $R_3=-\int_T^\infty\psi_2\Phi''\,du$ with $\Phi''=6Z/u^4-20Z^2/u^6$. So $|R_3|\le\frac1{12}(2Z/T^3+4Z^2/T^5)<\frac1{12}(16+128\Lambda)\le12\Lambda$.
\item $R_4=-2\sum_{k<K_0}\int_T^{R_k}\psi_2G_k''\,du$ with $G_k''=6Z/u^4$ and $\int_T^\infty6Zu^{-4}\,du=2Z/T^3<16$. So $|R_4|\le\frac2{12}K_0\cdot16<\frac{32}3\Lambda$.
\item $R_5=2\sum_{k<K_0}\psi_2(R_k)G_k'(R_k)$ with $G_k'(R_k)=-2Z/R_k^3=-2k^{3/2}/\sqrt Z$. Since $k<4\Lambda$, $\sum_{k<K_0}k^{3/2}<4\Lambda\cdot8\Lambda^{3/2}$, and with $\sqrt Z=\Lambda^{3/2}$ we get $|R_5|\le\frac2{12}\cdot2\cdot32\Lambda=\frac{32}3\Lambda$. These are the kinks of the $G_k$ at the points $R_k$. Summing over the $K_0\asymp Z^{1/3}$ values of $k$ is what produces the exponent $\frac13$.
\end{itemize}
Using $\Lambda\ge1$, the total is at most $(\frac18+\frac{272}{12}+12+\frac{32}3+\frac{32}3)\Lambda=\frac{449}8\Lambda<57\Lambda$, which proves~\eqref{eq:b2}.

(c) Fix $q$. The function $\kappa_q$ is multiplicative with $\kappa_q(p)=p^2/(p^2-2)$ for $p\nmid q$, $\kappa_q(p)=0$ for $p\mid q$ and $\kappa_q(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$. Let $\beta=\mu*\kappa_q$, so that $\kappa_q=1*\beta$. Then $\beta$ is multiplicative, with $\beta(p^j)=\kappa_q(p^j)-\kappa_q(p^{j-1})$:
\begin{itemize}
\item for $p\mid q$: $\beta(p)=-1$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge2$;
\item for $p\nmid q$: $\beta(p)=\frac2{p^2-2}$, $\beta(p^2)=-\frac{p^2}{p^2-2}$ and $\beta(p^j)=0$ for $j\ge3$.
\end{itemize}
\emph{Absolute convergence.} For $p\nmid q$, $\sum_j|\beta(p^j)|p^{-2j/3}\le\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}$, because $p^2/(p^2-2)\le2$. Hence
\[
\Sigma_{2/3}:=\sum_{n\ge1}\frac{|\beta(n)|}{n^{2/3}}\le\prod_{p\mid q}\bigl(1+p^{-2/3}\bigr)\prod_p\Bigl(1+\frac{2p^{-2/3}}{p^2-2}+2p^{-4/3}\Bigr)\le C_\beta\,2^{\omega(q)}\le C_\beta C(\eps)q^\eps,
\]
with an absolute constant $C_\beta$, by \cref{lem:divisor}. Similarly $\sum_n|\beta(n)|/n<\infty$ for each fixed $q$.

\emph{Rearrangement.} For $W>0$, $\sum_mB(W/m^2)\le\sum_m\min(\frac14,W/m^2)\le3\sqrt W$. Indeed, for $W<1$ the sum is at most $\zeta(2)W\le2\sqrt W$, and for $W\ge1$ it is at most $\frac14\sqrt W+W\cdot2/\sqrt W$ by \cref{lem:tail}. Hence $\sum_{n,m}|\beta(n)|B(Z/(nm)^2)\le3\sqrt Z\sum_n|\beta(n)|/n<\infty$, and we may rearrange:
\[
\sum_{t\ge1}\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)=\sum_{n,m\ge1}\beta(n)B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr)=\sum_{n\ge1}\beta(n)\sum_{m\ge1}B\Bigl(\frac{Z/n^2}{m^2}\Bigr).
\]
\emph{Main term.} Part (b) holds for every positive argument. Applying it with $Z/n^2$ in place of $Z$, and using $I\sqrt{Z/n^2}=I\sqrt Z/n$,
\[
\Bigl|\sum_t\kappa_q(t)B(Z/t^2)-I\sqrt Z\sum_n\frac{\beta(n)}n\Bigr|\le c_1\sum_n|\beta(n)|\Bigl(\frac Z{n^2}\Bigr)^{1/3}=c_1\Sigma_{2/3}Z^{1/3}.
\]
\emph{The constant.} By~\eqref{eq:euler}, $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\prod_p\bigl(1+\beta(p)/p+\beta(p^2)/p^2\bigr)$. For $p\mid q$ the factor is $1-1/p$. For $p\nmid q$ it is
\[
1+\frac2{p(p^2-2)}-\frac1{p^2-2}=\frac{p^3-3p+2}{p(p^2-2)}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p(p^2-2)}=\Bigl(1-\frac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\frac p{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
Hence $\sum_n\beta(n)/n=\Delta_q$, and (c) holds with $c_5(\eps)=c_1C_\beta C(\eps)$.
\end{proof}

\subsection{The main term for one modulus}

\begin{proposition}[Asymptotics of $\MT$]\label{prop:MT}
For every $\eps>0$ there is $c_6(\eps)$ such that for all real $x>0$ and all $q\in\N$,
\[
\bigl|\MT(x;q)-h(q)\sqrt{xq}\bigr|\le c_6(\eps)\,x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps},
\]
with $h$ as in~\eqref{eq:h}. In particular this holds for $x\ge1$ and $1\le q\le x$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
\emph{Factorising $t$.} Fix $q$. Every squarefree $t$ factors uniquely as $t=t_0t_1t_2$, where $t_0$ is composed of primes $p\nmid q$, $t_1$ of primes $p\,\|\,q$, and $t_2$ of primes $p$ with $p^2\mid q$. Conversely, every such triple of squarefree numbers gives a squarefree $t$. Let $\mathcal S_1$ and $\mathcal S_2$ be the finite sets of admissible $t_1$ and $t_2$ (all of them divide $q$). For squarefree $t$, $\gcd(t^2,q)=\prod_{p\mid t}p^{\min(2,v_p(q))}=t_1t_2^2$, so
\[
m_t(q)=t_0^2t_1,\qquad\frac x{q\,m_t(q)}=\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\quad\text{with}\quad Z_1=\frac{x}{q\,t_1},\qquad \eta(t)m_t(q)=\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\kappa(t_0).
\]
By the absolute convergence in \cref{lem:eta} we may regroup:
\[
\MT(x;q)=A_0\,q\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_1)\eta(t_2)\,t_1\,\Sigma(t_1),\qquad\Sigma(t_1)=\sum_{t_0\ge1}\kappa_q(t_0)B\Bigl(\frac{Z_1}{t_0^2}\Bigr).
\]
\emph{Applying \cref{prop:sawtooth}(c).} With $Z=Z_1>0$ we get $\Sigma(t_1)=\Delta_qI\sqrt{Z_1}+\theta\,c_5(\eps)q^\eps Z_1^{1/3}$. Since $t_1\sqrt{Z_1}=\sqrt{x/q}\,t_1^{1/2}$ and $t_1Z_1^{1/3}=(x/q)^{1/3}t_1^{2/3}$,
\[
\MT(x;q)=A_0\Delta_qI\sqrt{xq}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)+R,
\]
\[
|R|\le c_5(\eps)\,q^{1+\eps}\Bigl(\frac xq\Bigr)^{1/3}\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2),
\]
where we used $A_0\le1$. By~\eqref{eq:eta-bound}, $\sum_{t_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{2/3}\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-4/3})$ and $\sum_{t_2}\eta(t_2)\le\prod_p(1+2p^{-2})$, both absolute constants. So $|R|\le c_6(\eps)x^{1/3}q^{2/3+\eps}$.

\emph{The constant is $h(q)$.} The two finite sums are Euler products over the primes dividing $q$:
\[
\sum_{t_1\in\mathcal S_1}\eta(t_1)t_1^{1/2}=\prod_{p\|q}\Bigl(1+\frac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr),\qquad\sum_{t_2\in\mathcal S_2}\eta(t_2)=\prod_{p^2\mid q}\Bigl(1+\frac1{p^2-2}\Bigr).
\]
Multiplying the absolutely convergent products $A_0$ and $\Delta_q$ factor by factor, the local factor at $p$ of the main coefficient is
\begin{align*}
p\nmid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac p{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2+p-2)}{p^3}=\frac{(p-1)^2(p+2)}{p^3}=a_p,\\
p\,\|\,q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac{\sqrt p}{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-2+\sqrt p)}{p^3}=b_p,\\
p^2\mid q:&\quad\Bigl(1-\tfrac2{p^2}\Bigr)\Bigl(1-\tfrac1p\Bigr)\Bigl(1+\tfrac1{p^2-2}\Bigr)=\frac{(p-1)(p^2-1)}{p^3}=c_p .
\end{align*}
Together with the factor $I$, this is exactly $h(q)$.
\end{proof}

\begin{remark}
Since $b_p/a_p\ge1-1/p$ and $c_p/a_p=(p+1)/(p+2)\ge1-1/p$, we have $h(q)\ge IA_h\,\varphi(q)/q\gg_\eps q^{-\eps}$, where $A_h=\prod_pa_p>0$ (\cref{prop:poly}(0)). So \cref{prop:MT} gives, for real $x\ge1$ and integers $1\le q\le x$,
\[
\MT(x;q)=h(q)\sqrt{xq}\,\bigl(1+O_\eps(x^{2\eps}(q/x)^{1/6})\bigr).
\]
Here the restriction $q\le x$ is needed: the bound of \cref{prop:MT} gives the relative error $O_\eps\bigl(q^{2\eps}(q/x)^{1/6}\bigr)$, and $q^{2\eps}$ is replaced by $x^{2\eps}$. The display is false without it. For example, for $q=1$ and $x\to0$ we have $\MT(x;1)=O(x)$ by \cref{lem:eta}, so $\MT(x;1)/(h(1)\sqrt x)\to0$, whereas for $\eps>\frac1{12}$ the right-hand side tends to $h(1)\sqrt{x}$ times $1$. The relative error is not small when $q\asymp x$. This is why the asymptotic formula of \cref{thm:main}(iii) requires $Y\le x^{1-\delta}$, whereas the error term in~(ii), which keeps $\MT$ unexpanded, has no such restriction. The numerical data in \cref{sec:numerics} suggest that, after summation over the moduli, the secondary term has relative size roughly proportional to $\sqrt{Y/x}$. That is consistent with, but sharper than, the proved bound.
\end{remark}

\section{Provenance}\label{app:provenance}

The mathematics in \cref{sec:prelim,sec:densities,sec:identity,sec:pairs,sec:sawtooth,sec:single,sec:poly,sec:assembly} is an edited presentation of an archived run of a multi-agent proof pipeline in which language models proposed, proved and refereed the results. This appendix records where the material comes from. A proposition-by-proposition map, with every editorial change and correction, is in \texttt{manuscript/changes.md}.

\emph{Archive.}
\begin{itemize}
\item Source repository: \url{https://gitlab.com/mshepherd/squarefree-numbers}, archive label \texttt{zt-neutral}.
\item Archive commit: \texttt{ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba}.
\item Harness commit: \texttt{33aadc609359221ba5d81664438bce5f658f561c}.
\item Revision recorded for all run stages: \texttt{8dfc53d01e56c9949c42061fdbe907a98a12a5d7}.
\end{itemize}

\emph{Models and roles (as recorded).} The model identifiers are those recorded in the archive. The command-line tool versions are not model-weight versions, and model versions beyond these identifiers are unknown.
\begin{itemize}[before=\raggedright]
\item Planning and probing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}; probing also \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5}.
\item Numerics: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} produced candidate computations. The \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} snapshot was accepted.
\item Proofs: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} (prover).
\item Refereeing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}. Each proposition was reviewed independently by both.
\item Integration (assembly audit): \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}, independently.
\end{itemize}
Claude models ran under Claude Code 2.1.309 and Codex models under codex-cli 0.166.0. This write-up was produced by \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} (Claude Code 2.1.311).

\emph{Workflow.} The problem statement restricts $f$ to $\Z[t]$. It asks for the asymptotic behaviour of $V_f(x,y)$ in as large a range of $f(y)\le x$ as can be justified, and it accepts a weaker range or error term provided it is correct. The weight $f'(k)$ and the class~\eqref{eq:f-hyp} of polynomials used here are those of the problem statement; neither was changed. The numerical candidates were computed before any plan existed, and one was accepted on computational grounds only, not because of its fitted constants. Eight proof plans were written, and the plan \texttt{simplest@claude-opus-5-5} was selected by the project owner. It splits the argument into nine propositions P1--P9. In this text, P1 is \cref{prop:densities}, P2 is \cref{prop:identity}, P3 is \cref{prop:pairs}, P4 is \cref{prop:trivial}, P5 is \cref{prop:sawtooth}, P6 is \cref{prop:MT}, P7 is \cref{prop:single}, P8 is \cref{prop:poly}, and P9 is \cref{thm:main} with its proof in \cref{sec:assembly}. All nine proofs passed both referees in the first round, with only cosmetic remarks. Both integrators found that the propositions compose to the stated theorem without loss and without interface mismatches. The project owner accepted the proof as correct and complete. A separate read-only operator audit found no substantive gap and listed local corrections, which are carried out in this write-up (see \texttt{changes.md}) together with the cosmetic points raised by the referees. Agreement between models is evidence, not certification; the arguments are reproduced here in full so that they can be checked directly.

\emph{Independent checks during the run.} Before acceptance, the operator compared both numerical candidates on overlapping rows and recomputed some rows by brute force. One integrator recomputed all $16$ rows for $k^2+1$ and $k^3+2$ at $x=250000$ by direct counting. The other computed $\sum f'(k)\MT(x;f(k))$ independently and compared it with the data. These checks are recorded in the archive. The computations in \cref{sec:numerics} were redone for this write-up as described there.

\emph{Literature.} The run used the papers supplied with the problem and literature up to 2010, with the single exception of Brüdern--Wooley~\cite{BruedernWooley2011}, which was supplied. The present text cites only works in the supplied corpus. See \texttt{README.md} for the limitations of the bibliography.

\section{Provenance}\label{app:provenance}

The mathematics in \cref{sec:prelim,sec:densities,sec:identity,sec:pairs,sec:sawtooth,sec:single,sec:poly,sec:assembly} is an edited presentation of an archived run of a multi-agent proof pipeline in which language models proposed, proved and refereed the results. This appendix records where the material comes from. A proposition-by-proposition map, with every editorial change and correction, is in \texttt{manuscript/changes.md}.

\emph{Archive.}
\begin{itemize}
\item Source repository: \url{https://gitlab.com/mshepherd/squarefree-numbers}, archive label \texttt{zt-neutral}.
\item Archive commit: \texttt{ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba}.
\item Harness commit: \texttt{33aadc609359221ba5d81664438bce5f658f561c}.
\item Revision recorded for all run stages: \texttt{8dfc53d01e56c9949c42061fdbe907a98a12a5d7}.
\end{itemize}

\emph{Models and roles (as recorded).} The model identifiers are those recorded in the archive. The command-line tool versions are not model-weight versions, and model versions beyond these identifiers are unknown.
\begin{itemize}[before=\raggedright]
\item Planning and probing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}; probing also \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5}.
\item Numerics: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} produced candidate computations. The \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol} snapshot was accepted.
\item Proofs: \texttt{claude-sonnet-5-5} (prover).
\item Refereeing: \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}. Each proposition was reviewed independently by both.
\item Integration (assembly audit): \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}, independently.
\end{itemize}
During the run, Claude models ran under Claude Code 2.1.309 and Codex models under codex-cli 0.166.0.

\emph{Write-up stage.} This text was written by \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} (Claude Code 2.1.311). The provenance record names two write-up referees, \texttt{claude-opus-5-5} and \texttt{codex:gpt-6.1-sol}, and lists codex-cli 0.166.0 for the latter at this stage. Each earlier version of the text was reviewed by both write-up referees and then revised; the present text is the third version. Some of the corrections listed below come from these write-up reviews.

\emph{Workflow.} The problem statement restricts $f$ to $\Z[t]$. It asks for the asymptotic behaviour of $V_f(x,y)$ in as large a range of $f(y)\le x$ as can be justified, and it accepts a weaker range or error term provided it is correct. The weight $f'(k)$ and the class~\eqref{eq:f-hyp} of polynomials used here are those of the problem statement; neither was changed. The numerical candidates were computed before any plan existed, and one was accepted on computational grounds only, not because of its fitted constants. Eight proof plans were written, and the plan \texttt{simplest@claude-opus-5-5} was selected by the project owner. It splits the argument into nine propositions P1--P9. In this text, P1 is \cref{prop:densities}, P2 is \cref{prop:identity}, P3 is \cref{prop:pairs}, P4 is \cref{prop:trivial}, P5 is \cref{prop:sawtooth}, P6 is \cref{prop:MT}, P7 is \cref{prop:single}, P8 is \cref{prop:poly}, and P9 is \cref{thm:main} with its proof in \cref{sec:assembly}. All nine proofs passed both referees in the first round, with only cosmetic remarks. Both integrators found that the propositions compose to the stated theorem without loss and without interface mismatches. The project owner accepted the proof as correct and complete. A separate read-only operator audit found no substantive gap and listed local corrections, which are carried out in this write-up (see \texttt{changes.md}) together with the cosmetic points raised by the referees. Agreement between models is evidence, not certification; the arguments are reproduced here in full so that they can be checked directly.

\emph{Independent checks during the run.} Before acceptance, the operator compared both numerical candidates on overlapping rows and recomputed some rows by brute force. One integrator recomputed all $16$ rows for $k^2+1$ and $k^3+2$ at $x=250000$ by direct counting. The other computed $\sum f'(k)\MT(x;f(k))$ independently and compared it with the data. These checks are recorded in the archive. The computations in \cref{sec:numerics} were redone for this write-up as described there.

\emph{Literature.} The run used the papers supplied with the problem and literature up to 2010, with the single exception of Brüdern--Wooley~\cite{BruedernWooley2011}, which was supplied. The present text cites only works in the supplied corpus. See \texttt{README.md} for the limitations of the bibliography.

# Manuscript: sparse variance of squarefree numbers to polynomial moduli

Files:

* `main.tex`: main file; `sections/*.tex`: the sections and appendices;
  `references.bib`: bibliography.
* `generated/`: every table fragment (`tab_*.tex`), plot data file (`fig_*.dat`),
  the macros for numbers quoted in the text (`macros.tex`), and the re-run
  snapshot output (`snapshot_rerun_results.json`). All of these are written by
  `reproduce.py`.
* `reproduce.py`: regenerates everything in `generated/` and writes
  `reproduction.json` (list of artifacts, their sources, parameters, fits,
  constants and checks).
* `changes.md`: map from the manuscript to the archived run, with notation
  changes, merged arguments, corrections and additions.

## Reproduction

Requirements (no installation or network access is needed or performed):
Python 3 with numpy, scipy, mpmath and sympy; `clang++` with C++17 support;
about 5 GB of free memory; roughly 12–15 minutes on a current laptop. The
run that produced the shipped artifacts records its own timings in
`reproduction.json` (`snapshot_rerun.seconds` for the snapshot re-run,
`snapshot_rerun.total_seconds_of_reproduce_py` for the whole script).

From the workspace root (the directory containing `source/` and `manuscript/`):

```sh
python3 manuscript/reproduce.py
```

This

1. checks the SHA-256 of `source/numerics/snapshot/compute.py` and
   `counts.cpp` against `source/numerics/accepted.json`, copies both into the
   scratch directory `scratch/reproduce-work/`, and runs `compute.py` there
   unchanged. That script compiles `counts.cpp` with
   `clang++ -O3 -std=c++17`, re-runs its validations, recomputes all
   11 sizes x = 2.5e5 … 2.56e8 for the three polynomials, and redoes the
   fits. The archived executable `counts` is not used;
2. compares the regenerated `results.json` with the archived one (recorded in
   `reproduction.json` under `snapshot_rerun`);
3. computes C_f (Euler products over p ≤ 1e7 with a rigorous tail bound;
   interval endpoints rounded outwards; a 40-digit recomputation for
   p ≤ 1e5 as a check of floating-point rounding), Vaughan's c_2, the
   exact-shape sums `Σ f'(k) MT(x; f(k))` and `Σ F(k) h(f(k))`, symbolic
   checks, a self-test of the exact identity (Proposition 4.1), and, for each
   row at the largest x, the range of δ for which it lies in the range of
   Theorem 1.1(iii);
4. checks the qualitative statements made in Section 10 against the data
   (the script stops with an error if one fails) and writes
   `manuscript/generated/*` (including `macros.tex`, which holds every number
   quoted in the prose of Section 10) and `manuscript/reproduction.json`.

Options: `--work DIR` selects another scratch directory. The script refuses to
delete a non-empty directory that it did not create. `--reuse-work` reuses a
`results.json` already present in the scratch directory instead of re-running
the snapshot (for quick iterations only).

## Compilation

```sh
cd manuscript
latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error -no-shell-escape main.tex
```

The build uses only standard TeX Live packages (amsmath/amsthm, thmtools,
mathtools, pgfplots, booktabs, enumitem, hyperref, cleveref, microtype) and
BibTeX with the `plainurl` style. No shell escape is needed. `reproduce.py`
must have been run first, because the text inputs `generated/macros.tex` and
the generated tables.

## Bibliography limitations

* All works cited are in the supplied corpus (`papers/`). No historical
  attribution is made for the pair-count estimate of Proposition 5.1, whose
  proof is self-contained; the only related remark (Section 5) quotes what
  BGPVW (1998, §1, p. 3) report about Evelyn and Linfoot, whose papers were
  not consulted and are not cited separately.
* Goldston–Vaughan (1997) and Vaughan (1998, I) are cited only for the
  attribution made by Brüdern–Wooley (2011, §1); their content was not used.
* The supplied Brüdern–Wooley PDF is a preprint without journal header
  (PDF creation date 2009). The venue (Quart. J. Math. 62 (2011), 289–305) is
  taken from `papers/INDEX.md`. For it and for
  Brüdern–Granville–Perelli–Vaughan–Wooley (1998), whose venue is also taken
  from `papers/INDEX.md`, no URL, DOI or arXiv identifier is given in the
  supplied material, and none could be verified without network access. The
  bibliography entries say so; no locator was invented.
* Montgomery–Vaughan (2007): Theorem 1.8/1.9, Theorem 1.12, (2.20) and
  Corollary 10.4 were checked in the supplied chapters. Appendix B (Euler–Maclaurin
  summation) is not in the supplied corpus; the manuscript proves the needed
  Euler–Maclaurin lemma directly.
* Earlier work on the squarefree variance (Orr, Warlimont, Croft) is mentioned
  only as quoted in Vaughan (2005) and is not cited separately.

## Manual requirements

None beyond running the two commands above in this order.

# Changes: from the archived run to the manuscript

This file maps every result in `main.tex` to its source in the archived run
(`source/`), records the two referee reports for each proposition, and lists
every notation change, merged argument, correction and addition.

Archive: `source/` (archive label `zt-neutral`, archive commit
`ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba`); selected plan
`simplest@claude-opus-5-5` (`source/plan.md`, `source/plan.json`).
For every proposition PN, `source/props/PN/review-v1-0.json` is the review by
`claude-opus-5-5` and `source/props/PN/review-v1-1.json` the review by
`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`. Both reviewers passed all nine propositions in round 1
(severities: none or cosmetic). The assembly/integration reports are
`source/report/assembly-claude-opus-5-5.md`,
`source/report/assembly-codex-gpt-6.1-sol.md`,
`source/report/integration-*.json` and `source/report/integration.json`.

The theorem is stated with exactly the strength, ranges, hypotheses and
error terms of the plan's main theorem and of P9. The weight `f'(k)` and the
class of `f` are unchanged. No proposition is used outside its stated range.
No mathematical change was made beyond the local corrections listed in §4.
They were identified by the run's referees, by the operator audit recorded in
`source/interventions.md` (2026-11-03 10:21), or by the two referees of the
first round of this write-up (`feedback/0.json`, `feedback/1.json`). None of
them weakens a statement or changes the main theorem. A few auxiliary
statements are stated slightly more strongly or more explicitly than in the
archived statement files; each such case is taken from the archived proof or
proved in full in the manuscript, and is listed in §4a. One auxiliary lemma
(Lemma 2.6) received an extra hypothesis that holds in every application
(§4, item 19).

## 1. Map of results

| Manuscript | Archived statement / proof | Reviews |
|---|---|---|
| Theorem 1.1 (i), (ii), (iii) | `plan.md` "Main theorem"; `props/P9/statement.md`, `props/P9/proof.md`; composition audited in both assembly reports | P9: `review-v1-0.json` (Opus, pass, none), `review-v1-1.json` (Sol, pass, none) |
| Theorem 1.1, positivity of C_f | `props/P8/statement.md` claim (0) | see P8 |
| Remark 1.2 (range) | `plan.md` "Range" paragraph; assembly reports §5 (Opus) and §4 (Sol) | — |
| Remark 1.3 (C_t = Vaughan's c_2) | `plan.md` consistency check 1; Opus assembly report §3 | — (numerical in the run; see §5 below) |
| Lemma 2.1 (tail bound) | P3 proof Step 0 `(*)`; also P1 proof (i), P4 proof (0), P5 proof (c) | P1, P3, P4, P5 |
| Lemma 2.2 (residue-class count) | P1 proof (i) (`source/props/P1/proof.md` line 14); P3 proof Step 2 (line 33) | P1, P3 |
| Lemma 2.3 (divisor bounds) | standard facts used in P3, P5(c), P8 §3.2–3.3; MV (2.20) as cited by the Sol referee of P3 | P3, P5, P8 |
| Euler products (2.1) | used throughout P1, P3, P5, P8; cited as MV Theorem 1.9 | — |
| Lemma 2.4 (η, κ, A_0) | P1(v) and its proof; P2 notation (absolute convergence of MT); P6 proof Step 0 | P1, P2, P6 |
| Lemma 2.5 (coprime pairs) | P1 proof (iv) (the product I(t)) and P3 proof Step 4 | P1, P3 |
| Lemma 2.6 (Euler–Maclaurin) | P5 proof §0, Lemma EM (`source/props/P5/proof.md` lines 9–11); hypothesis for b = ∞ corrected, see §4 item 19 | P5 |
| Proposition 3.1 | P1 (i)–(v) | P1: Opus pass/none; Sol pass/cosmetic |
| Lemma 3.2 | P4 proof (ii) Step 3, estimate (3) for all y > 0 (`source/props/P4/proof.md` lines 33–48); P4 proof (i) (line 13) is its case r = 1 | P4 |
| Proposition 3.3 | P4 (i), (ii); explicit c_0 from P4 proof "Conclusion" (line 68) | P4: Opus pass/none; Sol pass/none |
| Proposition 4.1 | P2 | P2: Opus pass/none; Sol pass/none |
| Proposition 5.1 | P3 | P3: Opus pass/cosmetic; Sol pass/none |
| Proposition 6.1 (a)–(c) | P5 (a)–(c); explicit c_1 = 60 from P5 proof (b) (line 37) | P5: Opus pass/none; Sol pass/none |
| Proposition 6.2 | P6; range x > 0, q ≥ 1 from P6 proof Step 2 (line 50) and "Conclusion" (line 71) | P6: Opus pass/none; Sol pass/cosmetic |
| Proposition 7.1 | P7 | P7: Opus pass/none; Sol pass/none |
| Proposition 8.1 (0), (a)–(c) | P8 | P8: Opus pass/cosmetic; Sol pass/cosmetic |
| Lemma 8.2 (local factors) | P8 proof §0 "Elementary identities" | P8 |
| Lemma 8.3 (root counts) | P8 proof §0 "The function ρ" | P8 |
| Lemma 8.4 (shape of F) | P8 proof §0 "Shape of F" | P8 |
| Lemma 8.5 (monotone weights) | P8 proof §3.4 "Lemma" | P8 |
| Section 9 | P9 proof §0–§3 | P9 |
| Section 10 | `source/numerics/` (accepted snapshot `snapshot-nu6pbkr4`, candidate `codex-gpt-6.1-sol`), assembly reports §3–§4 (Opus) and §6 (Sol); recomputed by `manuscript/reproduce.py` | — |
| Appendix B | `provenance.json`, `source/interventions.md` | — |

## 2. Notation changes

| Archived | Manuscript | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| `tau_p` (local factor of C_f; plan, P8, P9, reports) | `σ_p` | `τ(n)` is the divisor function (P3, P8) |
| `c_0 = -4ζ(-1/2)` (P8 proof) | `I` (as in P5) | one name for one constant; `c_0` is now the absolute constant `3e^{2ζ(3/2)}` of P4 |
| `A_p, B_p, D_p` (P8 proof) | `a_p, b_p, c_p` (as in the Sol assembly report) | `B` is the sawtooth function |
| `A = ∏ A_p`, `b(q)`, `u = b*μ` (P8 proof) | `A_h`, `h^♮(q)`, `w = μ*h^♮` | avoid clashes with `A(m)`, `b_p` and P5's `b` |
| `c_1, c_2, c_3, c_5` (P8 shape constants), `C_1 = ∏_{p∈P_0} p^2`, truncation parameter `E` | `γ_1, …, γ_4`, `C_P`, `W` | avoid clashes with `c_1 = 60` (P5), `C_1` (Vaughan) and `E(x;q,l)` |
| `δ_q` (P5) | `Δ_q` | `δ` is the range parameter of the theorem |
| `f(t) = κ(t)1[(t,q)=1]`, `b = μ*f` (P5(c) proof) | `κ_q(t)`, `β = μ*κ_q` (the plan's name) | `f` is the polynomial |
| `A(u)`, `E_1, …, E_5` (P5(b) proof) | `Φ(u)`, `R_1, …, R_5` | `A(m)`, `E(x;q,l)` |
| `t = t_1 t_2 t_3`, `Z(t_2)` (P6 proof) | `t = t_0 t_1 t_2` (subscript = min(v_p(q), 2)), `Z_1` | mnemonic indexing |
| local `h(p)` (P1 proof (iii)) | `u(p)` | `h(q)` is the main-term function |
| `κ_r` (P4 proof) | `ν_r` | `κ(t)` |
| `E_1, E_2, E_3` (P3 proof) | `𝓔_1, 𝓔_2, 𝓔_3` | `E(x;q,l)` |
| generic `c(ε)` in P3, P5, P6, P7, P8 | `c_3(ε)`, `c_5(ε)`, `c_6(ε)`, `c_7(ε)`, `c_8(f), c_8(f,ε)` | to compose constants explicitly in §7 and §9 |
| Vaughan's modulus bound `Q` in `V(x,Q)` (Vaughan 2005, quoted in §1.2) | `Y`, so `V(x,Y)` | `Q(x)` and `Q(x;q,l)` are the counting functions (write-up referee, round 1) |
| actual ratio `ratio_actual` (snapshot) | `ϱ = f(y)/x` (§10.5) | distinguish from the target ratio `r` |

## 3. Merged arguments

* **Tail bound** `Σ_{a>w} a^{-2} ≤ 2/w`: proved four times in the archive (P1 (i),
  P3 `(*)`, P4 (0), P5 (c)); stated once as Lemma 2.1 (P3's version, valid for all w > 0).
* **Counting integers in a residue class** (`N/L + θ`): P1 (i) and P3 Step 2 →
  Lemma 2.2.
* **Coprime pairs of squarefree numbers**: the Euler product
  `Σ μ(a)μ(b)/(ab)^2 = ∏_{p∤e}(1-2/p^2)` was derived twice by "local choices"
  (P1 proof (iv), P3 proof Step 4). Lemma 2.5 states it once. Its proof groups
  the pairs by n = ab, which turns the sum into the multiplicative series
  `Σ μ(n)2^{ω(n)} n^{-2} 1[(n,e)=1]`. This is the same computation in a
  shorter form.
* **Squarefree numbers coprime to r**: P4 (i) (count of Q(x)) and P4 (ii) Step 3
  (count of T_r) are the same estimate; Lemma 3.2 proves the general case, and
  Proposition 3.3(i) is its case r = 1. The constant `3√x` of P4 (i) is unchanged.
* **Facts on η, κ, A_0** scattered over P1, P2, P6 → Lemma 2.4.

## 4. Corrections (all local; no weakening of any statement)

1. **P1(iii), normalisation** (Sol review of P1, "other issues"; operator audit).
   The proof states `q·μ(d) g_d/d²·1[g_d | n] = ∏_{p|d} h(p)`, with an
   extraneous factor q. Corrected in Proposition 3.1(iii): `μ(d) g_d/d² 1[g_d|n]
   = ∏_{p|d} u(p)` and `q g(q,n) = Σ_d μ²(d) ∏_{p|d} u(p)`.
2. **P1(iii), convergence** (Sol review of P1, main objection, cosmetic;
   operator audit). The claim `Σ_p |h(p)| ≤ Σ_p p^{-2}` is false for p | q
   (e.g. q = n = 2). Corrected: `|u(p)| = p^{-2}` for p ∤ q, and `|u(p)| ≤ 1` for
   the finitely many p | q, so the series converges absolutely.
3. **P3 Step 3, constant** (Opus review of P3). The proof writes
   `2·(π²/6)·Σ e^{-2}(2e/z) ≤ (4π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`; the left side equals
   `(2π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`. The original inequality was true but overestimated by a factor 2. The manuscript uses
   the correct value and the bound `7τ(m)/z` instead of `14τ(m)/z`. The final
   constant `(3 + 9C(ε))` replaces `2(1+τ*) + 1 + 14τ*`. Statement unchanged.
4. **P8 §3.4, endpoint k = 1** (Opus review of P8, cosmetic; operator audit;
   flagged as "P8 endpoint clarification" in `interventions.md`). The proof
   treats the closed first interval `[1, β]` as `(1-δ, β]`. That needs F to be defined and
   monotone left of 1, which fails e.g. for f = 3t − 1. Corrected by stating
   the counting lemma (Lemma 8.5) for arbitrary intervals (open, closed or
   half-open). Its proof only uses that `k_1 − e` and `k_n + e` lie outside the
   interval. The closed interval `[1, β]` is then covered directly, and the constant
   `3(2d−1) ≤ 6d` in eq. (8.10) (source eq. (3.9)) is unchanged.
5. **P8 §3.5, implicit error term** (Opus review of P8). The source writes
   `O(Y^{3/2} y^{-1/2})` for the term `(2/3)(Y^{3/2} − f(1)^{3/2})·O(y^{-1/2})`
   without saying where it comes from. The assembly display in §8.3 now shows
   it. The short-sum bound keeps the factor `(1 + log W)` (P8 (3.6)) explicitly,
   and it is absorbed by the choice `ε ≤ 1/8` (the source absorbs it into
   `E^{2ε}`). The final bound is unchanged.
6. **P8 §3.2(ii), constant dependence** (Opus review of P8). The bound
   `(2d)^{ω(n)} ≤ C n^ε` has a constant depending on d; this is now stated
   (`C(f, ε)`).
7. **P2, wording** (Opus review of P2). The parenthetical after (3) ("finitely
   many nonzero terms after the bracket is rewritten") is replaced by: the
   bracket vanishes for `q m_t(q) > x` (twice an empty sum), and each of the
   three series obtained by splitting it converges absolutely.
8. **P4 (i), wording** (Opus review of P4). "Every squarefree-indicator
   identity gives" → derived from `μ²(n) = Σ_{d²|n} μ(d)` (Lemma 3.2).
9. **P5(b), small s** (Opus review of P5). The two quantities both lie in
   `[0, Λ/4]`, so their difference is at most `Λ/4` (source: `Λ/2`). The constant
   `c_1 = 60` is kept.
10. **P9, real-variable hypothesis** (Opus review of P9). The step
    `f(k) ≤ f(y)` for real y uses `f'(t) ≥ 1` for all real `t ≥ 1`. This is
    now explicit in (1.1) and in §9. The convention `1 ≤ k ≤ y` (integers) is
    explicit in (1.2). The constants `c(ε/3)`, `c(f, ε/3)` and their
    combination are written out in §9.
11. **P9 remark on δ < 1/9** (Opus review of P9). Non-emptiness of the range
    holds for x > 1; stated so.
12. **P7, role of x ≥ 2** (Opus review of P7). Noted in the proof of
    Proposition 7.1 that x ≥ 2 is needed only for P3.
13. **P3, n ≥ 1** (Opus review of P3). C_x(m) counts positive n; explicit in
    eq. (4.1).
14. **P1(iii), sign of n** (Opus review of P1). Stated for squarefree `n ∈ ℕ`,
    the only case used.
15. **P5, citation "MV Thm B.5"** (Opus review of P5: not found in the
    supplied PDF). Appendix B of Montgomery–Vaughan is not in the supplied
    corpus. Its §1.3 refers to "Theorem B.5" for Euler–Maclaurin summation.
    The manuscript proves Lemma 2.6 directly and cites only MV §1.3 and
    Theorem 1.12 for comparison.
16. **Unused numerical notes in the proofs** (not reproduced):
    * P2: the proof's check agreed only to ~1e-3 because of truncation (Opus
      review); replaced by the exact self-test in `reproduce.py`
      (`identity_selftest`, agreement 4.8e-10).
    * P6: the tail estimate `A_0 x/(q·3000)` wrongly contains 1/q (Sol review),
      and the difference 92 at (10^6, 1) is a truncation artefact (Opus review).
    * P8: "ρ(p²) ≈ ρ(p)/p, exact for these squarefree f" is false for root
      counts (should be ρ(p²) = ρ(p) for unramified p); Sol review and Sol
      assembly report §5. Also flagged in the operator audit.
    * P1, P5: numerical sanity checks are not reproduced; P5's constants were
      checked by the referees.
17. **Remark 1.2 (range of part (ii))**. The plan says statement (a)/(ii)
    "remains meaningful up to f(y) ~ x". The manuscript states only what is
    proved: the error term of (ii) is of smaller order than `x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}`
    for `x^{7/9+δ} ≤ Y ≤ x`. No lower bound for `Σ f'(k) MT(x; f(k))` is
    claimed.
18. **References.** P8's "Hooley 1964 (background on rho only; not needed)" is
    dropped because no statement from it is used. The plan named a 1949 paper
    of Mirsky on pairs of squarefree numbers from memory. Earlier versions of
    this write-up cited Mirsky, Bull. AMS 55 (1949), from
    `bibliography-candidates.json`, without having consulted it. Following the
    round-1 write-up review (`feedback/0.json`, issue 7), that unverifiable
    historical attribution is dropped. Section 5 now quotes only what the
    supplied BGPVW (1998, §1) says about the related additive problem (see §5).
19. **Lemma 2.6 / P5 Lemma EM, the case b = ∞** (write-up referee
    `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, round 1, `feedback/1.json` issue 1). P5 proof line 11
    states the infinite-interval formula under `F, F' → 0`, `F'' ∈ L^1`. That is
    not enough: `G(u) = cos(log u)/u` on `[1, ∞)` satisfies these conditions,
    but its integral diverges. The manuscript adds the hypothesis that
    `∫_a^∞ G` converges, proves the limit passage, and notes that every
    application satisfies it: `G(u) = u^{-s}` with `Re s > 1` in Proposition
    6.1(a) (P5 line 23), and `Φ(u) = Z/u² − Z²/u⁴` on `(T, ∞)` in Proposition
    6.1(b) (P5 line 53). The argument of P5, and hence every statement, is
    unaffected. This makes explicit a hypothesis that holds in every use; it is
    not a repair of a gap in the argument.
20. **Proposition 6.1(b), arithmetic of the final sum** (write-up referee
    `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, round 1, issue 2). The round-1 manuscript wrote the
    sum of the bounds for `R_1, …, R_5` as `< 56.1Λ`. It equals
    `449/8 Λ = 56.125Λ`. This was an error introduced in the write-up: the
    archived P5 proof (line 65) has the correct bound `< 57Λ`, with the
    decimal approximation "56.1" written as a rounding. Corrected to
    `= 449/8 Λ < 57Λ`. The constant `c_1 = 60` is unchanged.

## 4a. Statements stated more explicitly or more strongly than the archived statement files

Each item is either proved in the archived proof (with line reference) or
proved in full in the manuscript. None is used to strengthen the main theorem.
(Identified as unrecorded in the round-1 write-up review, `feedback/0.json`,
issue 2.)

* **Proposition 6.2 (P6), range.** `source/props/P6/statement.md` states the
  bound for real `x ≥ 1` and integers `1 ≤ q ≤ x`. The manuscript states it
  for all real `x > 0` and all `q ∈ ℕ`, adding "in particular for `x ≥ 1`,
  `1 ≤ q ≤ x`". Source: P6 proof Step 2, line 50 ("No use was made of q ≤ x or
  x ≥ 1 in this step; the error bound holds for all x > 0, q ≥ 1"), and the
  Conclusion, line 71.
* **Proposition 6.1(b) (P5(b)), explicit constant.** The statement file has
  "an absolute constant c_1"; the manuscript states `c_1 = 60`. Source: P5
  proof line 37 ("I show this with c_1 = 60").
* **Proposition 3.3 (P4), explicit constant.** The statement file has "an

# Changes: from the archived run to the manuscript

This file maps every result in `main.tex` to its source in the archived run
(`source/`), records the two referee reports for each proposition, and lists
every notation change, merged argument, correction and addition.

Archive: `source/` (archive label `zt-neutral`, archive commit
`ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba`); selected plan
`simplest@claude-opus-5-5` (`source/plan.md`, `source/plan.json`).
For every proposition PN, `source/props/PN/review-v1-0.json` is the review by
`claude-opus-5-5` and `source/props/PN/review-v1-1.json` the review by
`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`. Both reviewers passed all nine propositions in round 1
(severities: none or cosmetic). The assembly/integration reports are
`source/report/assembly-claude-opus-5-5.md`,
`source/report/assembly-codex-gpt-6.1-sol.md`,
`source/report/integration-*.json` and `source/report/integration.json`.

The theorem is stated with exactly the strength, ranges, hypotheses and
error terms of the plan's main theorem and of P9. The weight `f'(k)` and the
class of `f` are unchanged. No proposition is used outside its stated range.
No mathematical change was made beyond the local corrections listed in §4.
Each was identified by one of the following:

* the run's referees (`source/props/*/review-v1-*.json`);
* the operator audit recorded in `source/interventions.md` (2026-11-03 10:21),
  whose corrections are also named in the owner's "result" entry of 2026-11-03;
* the write-up referees, `claude-opus-5-5` and `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, after the
  run.

None of them weakens a statement or changes the main theorem. A few auxiliary
statements are stated slightly more strongly or more explicitly than in the
archived statement files. Each such case is taken from the archived proof or
proved in full in the manuscript, and is listed in §4a. One auxiliary lemma
(Lemma 2.6) received an extra hypothesis that holds in every application
(§4, item 19). That correction came from the write-up review, is not covered
by the owner's recorded decision, and is **flagged for Markus's
acknowledgement**.

**Write-up review files.** The write-up went through two review rounds
before this version. Both reports of each round are cited by round below:

* **Round 1** reports: these were `feedback/0.json` (`claude-opus-5-5`) and
  `feedback/1.json` (`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`) in the round-2 writer's workspace.
  They are *not* part of the present workspace, so references to them cannot
  be checked against the original files here. Each objection is restated
  inline below, in the round-2 writer's summary.
* **Round 2** reports: these are the files `feedback/0.json`
  (`claude-opus-5-5`, run `writeup-referee-zt-neutral-r2-0-…`) and
  `feedback/1.json` (`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, run
  `writeup-referee-zt-neutral-r2-1-…`) supplied with this version. Both
  verdicts are "revise". Both found no gap in the source argument and no
  change to the accepted mathematics. Their objections and the responses are
  in §8.

## 2. Notation changes

## 3. Merged arguments

* **Tail bound** `Σ_{a>w} a^{-2} ≤ 2/w`: proved four times in the archive (P1 (i),
  P3 `(*)`, P4 (0), P5 (c)); stated once as Lemma 2.1 (P3's version, valid for all w > 0).
* **Counting integers in a residue class** (`N/L + θ`): P1 (i) and P3 Step 2 →
  Lemma 2.2.
* **Coprime pairs of squarefree numbers**: the Euler product
  `Σ μ(a)μ(b)/(ab)^2 = ∏_{p∤e}(1-2/p^2)` was derived twice by "local choices"
  (P1 proof (iv), P3 proof Step 4). Lemma 2.5 states it once. Its proof groups
  the pairs by n = ab, which turns the sum into the multiplicative series
  `Σ μ(n)2^{ω(n)} n^{-2} 1[(n,e)=1]`. This is the same computation in a
  shorter form.
* **Squarefree numbers coprime to r**: P4 (i) (count of Q(x)) and P4 (ii) Step 3
  (count of T_r) are the same estimate; Lemma 3.2 proves the general case, and
  Proposition 3.3(i) is its case r = 1. The constant `3√x` of P4 (i) is unchanged.
* **Facts on η, κ, A_0** scattered over P1, P2, P6 → Lemma 2.4.

## 4. Corrections (all local; no weakening of any statement)

1. **P1(iii), normalisation** (Sol review of P1, "other issues"; operator audit).
   The proof states `q·μ(d) g_d/d²·1[g_d | n] = ∏_{p|d} h(p)`, with an
   extraneous factor q. Corrected in Proposition 3.1(iii): `μ(d) g_d/d² 1[g_d|n]
   = ∏_{p|d} u(p)` and `q g(q,n) = Σ_d μ²(d) ∏_{p|d} u(p)`.
2. **P1(iii), convergence** (Sol review of P1, main objection, cosmetic;
   operator audit). The claim `Σ_p |h(p)| ≤ Σ_p p^{-2}` is false for p | q
   (e.g. q = n = 2). Corrected: `|u(p)| = p^{-2}` for p ∤ q, and `|u(p)| ≤ 1` for
   the finitely many p | q, so the series converges absolutely.
3. **P3 Step 3, constant** (Opus review of P3). The proof writes
   `2·(π²/6)·Σ e^{-2}(2e/z) ≤ (4π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`; the left side equals
   `(2π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`. The original inequality was true but overestimated by a factor 2. The manuscript uses
   the correct value and the bound `7τ(m)/z` instead of `14τ(m)/z`. The final
   constant `(3 + 9C(ε))` replaces `2(1+τ*) + 1 + 14τ*`. Statement unchanged.
4. **P8 §3.4, endpoint k = 1** (Opus review of P8, cosmetic; operator audit;
   flagged as "P8 endpoint clarification" in `interventions.md`). The proof
   treats the closed first interval `[1, β]` as `(1-δ, β]`. That needs F to be defined and
   monotone left of 1, which fails e.g. for f = 3t − 1. Corrected by stating
   the counting lemma (Lemma 8.5) for arbitrary intervals (open, closed or
   half-open). Its proof only uses that `k_1 − e` and `k_n + e` lie outside the
   interval. The closed interval `[1, β]` is then covered directly, and the constant
   `3(2d−1) ≤ 6d` in eq. (8.10) (source eq. (3.9)) is unchanged.
5. **P8 §3.5, implicit error term** (Opus review of P8). The source writes
   `O(Y^{3/2} y^{-1/2})` for the term `(2/3)(Y^{3/2} − f(1)^{3/2})·O(y^{-1/2})`
   without saying where it comes from. The assembly display in §8.3 now shows
   it. The short-sum bound keeps the factor `(1 + log W)` (P8 (3.6)) explicitly,
   and it is absorbed by the choice `ε ≤ 1/8` (the source absorbs it into
   `E^{2ε}`). The final bound is unchanged.
6. **P8 §3.2(ii), constant dependence** (Opus review of P8). The bound
   `(2d)^{ω(n)} ≤ C n^ε` has a constant depending on d; this is now stated
   (`C(f, ε)`).
7. **P2, wording** (Opus review of P2). The parenthetical after (3) ("finitely
   many nonzero terms after the bracket is rewritten") is replaced by: the
   bracket vanishes for `q m_t(q) > x` (twice an empty sum), and each of the
   three series obtained by splitting it converges absolutely.
8. **P4 (i), wording** (Opus review of P4). "Every squarefree-indicator
   identity gives" → derived from `μ²(n) = Σ_{d²|n} μ(d)` (Lemma 3.2).
9. **P5(b), small s** (Opus review of P5). The two quantities both lie in
   `[0, Λ/4]`, so their difference is at most `Λ/4` (source: `Λ/2`). The constant
   `c_1 = 60` is kept.
10. **P9, real-variable hypothesis** (Opus review of P9). The step
    `f(k) ≤ f(y)` for real y uses `f'(t) ≥ 1` for all real `t ≥ 1`. This is
    now explicit in (1.1) and in §9. The convention `1 ≤ k ≤ y` (integers) is
    explicit in (1.2). The constants `c(ε/3)`, `c(f, ε/3)` and their
    combination are written out in §9.
11. **P9 remark on δ < 1/9** (Opus review of P9). Non-emptiness of the range
    holds for x > 1; stated so.
12. **P7, role of x ≥ 2** (Opus review of P7). Noted in the proof of
    Proposition 7.1 that x ≥ 2 is needed only for P3.
13. **P3, n ≥ 1** (Opus review of P3). C_x(m) counts positive n; explicit in
    eq. (4.1).
14. **P1(iii), sign of n** (Opus review of P1). Stated for squarefree `n ∈ ℕ`,
    the only case used.
15. **P5, citation "MV Thm B.5"** (Opus review of P5: not found in the
    supplied PDF). Appendix B of Montgomery–Vaughan is not in the supplied
    corpus. Its §1.3 refers to "Theorem B.5" for Euler–Maclaurin summation.
    The manuscript proves Lemma 2.6 directly and cites only MV §1.3 and
    Theorem 1.12 for comparison.
16. **Unused numerical notes in the proofs** (not reproduced):
    * P2: the proof's check agreed only to ~1e-3 because of truncation (Opus
      review); replaced by the exact self-test in `reproduce.py`
      (`identity_selftest`, agreement 4.8e-10).
    * P6: the tail estimate `A_0 x/(q·3000)` wrongly contains 1/q (Sol review),
      and the difference 92 at (10^6, 1) is a truncation artefact (Opus review).
    * P8: "ρ(p²) ≈ ρ(p)/p, exact for these squarefree f" is false for root
      counts (should be ρ(p²) = ρ(p) for unramified p); Sol review and Sol
      assembly report §5. Also flagged in the operator audit.
    * P1, P5: numerical sanity checks are not reproduced; P5's constants were
      checked by the referees.
17. **Remark 1.2 (range of part (ii))**. The plan says statement (a)/(ii)
    "remains meaningful up to f(y) ~ x". The manuscript states only what is
    proved: the error term of (ii) is of smaller order than `x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}`
    for `x^{7/9+δ} ≤ Y ≤ x`. No lower bound for `Σ f'(k) MT(x; f(k))` is
    claimed.
18. **References.** P8's "Hooley 1964 (background on rho only; not needed)" is
    dropped because no statement from it is used. The plan named a 1949 paper
    of Mirsky on pairs of squarefree numbers from memory. Earlier versions of
    this write-up cited Mirsky, Bull. AMS 55 (1949), from
    `bibliography-candidates.json`, without having consulted it. Following the
    round-1 write-up review (`feedback/0.json`, issue 7), that unverifiable
    historical attribution is dropped. Section 5 now quotes only what the
    supplied BGPVW (1998, §1) says about the related additive problem (see §5).
19. **Lemma 2.6 / P5 Lemma EM, the case b = ∞** (write-up referee
    `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, round 1, `feedback/1.json` issue 1). P5 proof line 11
    states the infinite-interval formula under `F, F' → 0`, `F'' ∈ L^1`. That is
    not enough: `G(u) = cos(log u)/u` on `[1, ∞)` satisfies these conditions,
    but its integral diverges. The manuscript adds the hypothesis that
    `∫_a^∞ G` converges, proves the limit passage, and notes that every
    application satisfies it: `G(u) = u^{-s}` with `Re s > 1` in Proposition
    6.1(a) (P5 line 23), and `Φ(u) = Z/u² − Z²/u⁴` on `(T, ∞)` in Proposition
    6.1(b) (P5 line 53). The argument of P5, and hence every statement, is
    unaffected. This makes explicit a hypothesis that holds in every use; it is
    not a repair of a gap in the argument.
20. **Proposition 6.1(b), arithmetic of the final sum** (write-up referee
    `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, round 1, issue 2). The round-1 manuscript wrote the
    sum of the bounds for `R_1, …, R_5` as `< 56.1Λ`. It equals
    `449/8 Λ = 56.125Λ`. This was an error introduced in the write-up: the
    archived P5 proof (line 65) has the correct bound `< 57Λ`, with the
    decimal approximation "56.1" written as a rounding. Corrected to
    `= 449/8 Λ < 57Λ`. The constant `c_1 = 60` is unchanged.

## 4a. Statements stated more explicitly or more strongly than the archived statement files

Each item is either proved in the archived proof (with line reference) or
proved in full in the manuscript. None is used to strengthen the main theorem.
(Identified as unrecorded in the round-1 write-up review, `feedback/0.json`,
issue 2.)

* **Proposition 6.2 (P6), range.** `source/props/P6/statement.md` states the
  bound for real `x ≥ 1` and integers `1 ≤ q ≤ x`. The manuscript states it
  for all real `x > 0` and all `q ∈ ℕ`, adding "in particular for `x ≥ 1`,
  `1 ≤ q ≤ x`". Source: P6 proof Step 2, line 50 ("No use was made of q ≤ x or
  x ≥ 1 in this step; the error bound holds for all x > 0, q ≥ 1"), and the
  Conclusion, line 71.
* **Proposition 6.1(b) (P5(b)), explicit constant.** The statement file has
  "an absolute constant c_1"; the manuscript states `c_1 = 60`. Source: P5
  proof line 37 ("I show this with c_1 = 60").
* **Proposition 3.3 (P4), explicit constant.** The statement file has "an
  absolute constant c_0"; the manuscript states `c_0 = 3e^{2ζ(3/2)}`. Source: P4
  proof line 68. The manuscript also notes, as in P4 proof line 17, that `q ≤ x`
  is not used in (ii).
* **Lemma 3.2 (P4 Step 3).** `|T_r(y) − ν_r y| ≤ 3·2^{ω(r)} √y` for all `y > 0` is
  P4 proof estimate (3), lines 45–48. Its case `r = 1`, `|Q(y) − 6y/π²| ≤ 3√y`
  for all `y > 0`, extends P4(i) (stated for `x ≥ 1`, line 13) to `0 < y < 1`.
  That case is trivial: `Q(y) = 0` and `6y/π² < 3√y`. It is not used.
* **Lemma 2.2, strict inequality.** P1 proof line 14 and P3 proof line 33 use
  `N/L + θ` with `|θ| ≤ 1`. Lemma 2.2 states and proves `|θ| < 1`. Every use
  needs only `|θ| ≤ 1`.
* **Proposition 5.1 (P3), constant.** `(3 + 9C(ε))` instead of
  `2(1+τ*) + 1 + 14τ*`; see §4 item 3.

## 5. Material added after the run

None of the following is used in a proof.

* **Section 1 background**: Vaughan's theorem for the full variance (2005,
  (1.12)–(1.16)), the earlier `x²𝓕(x/Y)` results it quotes, and the
  Brüdern–Wooley theorem (2011, Theorem in §1), all read from the supplied PDFs.
* **Section 5, first paragraph**: the remark that BGPVW (1998, §1) report an
  elementary argument of Evelyn and Linfoot giving
  `r_k(n) = S_k(n) n + O(n^{2/(k+1)+ε})` for sums of two k-free numbers (read
  from the supplied PDF, p. 3). It is background only.
* **Remark 1.3**: the identity `σ_p|_{ρ≡1} = C_{1,p}(1 − p^{-2})²` of local
  factors. The run checked `C_t = c_2` numerically to 7–8 digits (plan;
  Opus assembly report §3). The write-up verifies the identity symbolically
  with sympy (`reproduce.py`, `symbolic_local_identity`).
* **Section 10** is recomputed from scratch by `manuscript/reproduce.py`:
  * re-run of the accepted snapshot code (unchanged; recompiled), with
    an exact comparison against the archived `results.json` (identical);
  * C_f for k²+1, k³+2, 2k+1 and the formal f = t, with a rigorous bound for
    the omitted primes. This uses the tail argument of the Sol assembly report §6, eq. (21),
    which rests on eq. (8.2), `|σ_p − 1| ≤ (3+2d)/p²`, from P8 §1. The value for 2k+1
    (not compared by either integrator) is new here; the plan quotes 0.14261;
  * new code for `Σ f'(k) MT(x; f(k))` and `Σ F(k) h(f(k))`. The Opus integrator
    did a similar computation with its own code, which is not in the archive.
    The write-up's code evaluates the infinite t-series without truncation (closed-form tails)
    and is checked against the exact identity of Proposition 4.1;
  * the sensitivity table of the snapshot's extrapolation (values from the
    snapshot's own `results.json` fields);
  * (round 2) outward rounding of the printed C_f interval endpoints, the
    digits of C_f fixed by the intervals, and a 40-digit recomputation of the
    partial products for p ≤ 1e5 as a check of floating-point rounding;
  * (round 2) for every row at the largest x, the largest δ for which the row
    lies in the range of Theorem 1.1(iii), computed from the actual ratio
    f(y)/x (`reproduction.json`, `eligibility_at_largest_x`);
  * (round 2) every number quoted in the prose of Section 10 is generated as a
    macro by `reproduce.py`, and the qualitative claims made there are checked
    by the script (`reproduction.json`, `text_claim_checks`).
* **Remark 6.3**: the lower bound `h(q) ≥ I A_h φ(q)/q`, from `b_p/a_p ≥ 1 − 1/p`
  and `c_p/a_p = (p+1)/(p+2)`. It justifies stating the relative error of
  Proposition 6.2. This is a remark only; P6 states the absolute error.
* **Appendix B** (provenance), from `provenance.json` and `interventions.md`.

## 6. Exposure and compliance notes

No source outside the workspace was read. No work by the excluded author and
not the excluded paper was searched for, opened or used. The repository URL in
`provenance.json` is stated for reproducibility only and was not browsed. No
literature published after 2010 was used except the supplied
Brüdern–Wooley (2011) paper.

6. §10.4 tautology and the "0.140" wording: rewritten; the values at

# Changes: from the archived run to the manuscript

This file maps every result in `main.tex` to its source in the archived run
(`source/`), records the two referee reports for each proposition, and lists
every notation change, merged argument, correction and addition.

Archive: `source/` (archive label `zt-neutral`, archive commit
`ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba`); selected plan
`simplest@claude-opus-5-5` (`source/plan.md`, `source/plan.json`).
For every proposition PN, `source/props/PN/review-v1-0.json` is the review by
`claude-opus-5-5` and `source/props/PN/review-v1-1.json` the review by
`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`. Both reviewers passed all nine propositions in round 1
(severities: none or cosmetic). The assembly/integration reports are
`source/report/assembly-claude-opus-5-5.md`,
`source/report/assembly-codex-gpt-6.1-sol.md`,
`source/report/integration-*.json` and `source/report/integration.json`.

The theorem is stated with exactly the strength, ranges, hypotheses and
error terms of the plan's main theorem and of P9. The weight `f'(k)` and the
class of `f` are unchanged. No proposition is used outside its stated range.
No mathematical change was made beyond the local corrections listed in §4.
Each was identified by one of the following:

* the run's referees (`source/props/*/review-v1-*.json`);
* the operator audit recorded in `source/interventions.md` (2026-11-03 10:21),
  whose corrections are also named in the owner's "result" entry of 2026-11-03;
* the write-up referees, `claude-opus-5-5` and `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, after the
  run.

None of them weakens a statement or changes the main theorem. A few auxiliary
statements are stated slightly more strongly or more explicitly than in the
archived statement files. Each such case is taken from the archived proof or
proved in full in the manuscript, and is listed in §4a. One auxiliary lemma
(Lemma 2.6) received an extra hypothesis that holds in every application
(§4, item 19). That correction came from the write-up review, is not covered
by the owner's recorded decision, and is **flagged for Markus's
acknowledgement**.

**Write-up review files.** The write-up went through two review rounds
before this version. Both reports of each round are cited by round below:

* **Round 1** reports: these were `feedback/0.json` (`claude-opus-5-5`) and
  `feedback/1.json` (`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`) in the round-2 writer's workspace.
  They are *not* part of the present workspace, so references to them cannot

## 3. Merged arguments

* **Tail bound** `Σ_{a>w} a^{-2} ≤ 2/w`: proved four times in the archive (P1 (i),
  P3 `(*)`, P4 (0), P5 (c)); stated once as Lemma 2.1 (P3's version, valid for all w > 0).
* **Counting integers in a residue class** (`N/L + θ`): P1 (i) and P3 Step 2 →
  Lemma 2.2.
* **Coprime pairs of squarefree numbers**: the Euler product
  `Σ μ(a)μ(b)/(ab)^2 = ∏_{p∤e}(1-2/p^2)` was derived twice by "local choices"
  (P1 proof (iv), P3 proof Step 4). Lemma 2.5 states it once. Its proof groups
  the pairs by n = ab, which turns the sum into the multiplicative series
  `Σ μ(n)2^{ω(n)} n^{-2} 1[(n,e)=1]`. This is the same computation in a
  shorter form.
* **Squarefree numbers coprime to r**: P4 (i) (count of Q(x)) and P4 (ii) Step 3
  (count of T_r) are the same estimate; Lemma 3.2 proves the general case, and
  Proposition 3.3(i) is its case r = 1. The constant `3√x` of P4 (i) is unchanged.
* **Facts on η, κ, A_0** scattered over P1, P2, P6 → Lemma 2.4.

## 4. Corrections (all local; no weakening of any statement)

1. **P1(iii), normalisation** (Sol review of P1, "other issues"; operator audit).
   The proof states `q·μ(d) g_d/d²·1[g_d | n] = ∏_{p|d} h(p)`, with an
   extraneous factor q. Corrected in Proposition 3.1(iii): `μ(d) g_d/d² 1[g_d|n]
   = ∏_{p|d} u(p)` and `q g(q,n) = Σ_d μ²(d) ∏_{p|d} u(p)`.
2. **P1(iii), convergence** (Sol review of P1, main objection, cosmetic;
   operator audit). The claim `Σ_p |h(p)| ≤ Σ_p p^{-2}` is false for p | q
   (e.g. q = n = 2). Corrected: `|u(p)| = p^{-2}` for p ∤ q, and `|u(p)| ≤ 1` for
   the finitely many p | q, so the series converges absolutely.
3. **P3 Step 3, constant** (Opus review of P3). The proof writes
   `2·(π²/6)·Σ e^{-2}(2e/z) ≤ (4π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`; the left side equals
   `(2π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`. The original inequality was true but overestimated by a factor 2. The manuscript uses
   the correct value and the bound `7τ(m)/z` instead of `14τ(m)/z`. The final
   constant `(3 + 9C(ε))` replaces `2(1+τ*) + 1 + 14τ*`. Statement unchanged.
4. **P8 §3.4, endpoint k = 1** (Opus review of P8, cosmetic; operator audit;
   flagged as "P8 endpoint clarification" in `interventions.md`). The proof
   treats the closed first interval `[1, β]` as `(1-δ, β]`. That needs F to be defined and
   monotone left of 1, which fails e.g. for f = 3t − 1. Corrected by stating
   the counting lemma (Lemma 8.5) for arbitrary intervals (open, closed or
   half-open). Its proof only uses that `k_1 − e` and `k_n + e` lie outside the
   interval. The closed interval `[1, β]` is then covered directly, and the constant
   `3(2d−1) ≤ 6d` in eq. (8.10) (source eq. (3.9)) is unchanged.
5. **P8 §3.5, implicit error term** (Opus review of P8). The source writes
   `O(Y^{3/2} y^{-1/2})` for the term `(2/3)(Y^{3/2} − f(1)^{3/2})·O(y^{-1/2})`
   without saying where it comes from. The assembly display in §8.3 now shows
   it. The short-sum bound keeps the factor `(1 + log W)` (P8 (3.6)) explicitly,
   and it is absorbed by the choice `ε ≤ 1/8` (the source absorbs it into
   `E^{2ε}`). The final bound is unchanged.
6. **P8 §3.2(ii), constant dependence** (Opus review of P8). The bound
   `(2d)^{ω(n)} ≤ C n^ε` has a constant depending on d; this is now stated
   (`C(f, ε)`).
7. **P2, wording** (Opus review of P2). The parenthetical after (3) ("finitely
   many nonzero terms after the bracket is rewritten") is replaced by: the
   bracket vanishes for `q m_t(q) > x` (twice an empty sum), and each of the
   three series obtained by splitting it converges absolutely.
8. **P4 (i), wording** (Opus review of P4). "Every squarefree-indicator
   identity gives" → derived from `μ²(n) = Σ_{d²|n} μ(d)` (Lemma 3.2).
9. **P5(b), small s** (Opus review of P5). The two quantities both lie in
   `[0, Λ/4]`, so their difference is at most `Λ/4` (source: `Λ/2`). The constant
   `c_1 = 60` is kept.
10. **P9, real-variable hypothesis** (Opus review of P9). The step
    `f(k) ≤ f(y)` for real y uses `f'(t) ≥ 1` for all real `t ≥ 1`. This is

11. **P9 remark on δ < 1/9** (Opus review of P9). Non-emptiness of the range

12. **P7, role of x ≥ 2** (Opus review of P7). Noted in the proof of

13. **P3, n ≥ 1** (Opus review of P3). C_x(m) counts positive n; explicit in

14. **P1(iii), sign of n** (Opus review of P1). Stated for squarefree `n ∈ ℕ`,

15. **P5, citation "MV Thm B.5"** (Opus review of P5: not found in the

19. **Lemma 2.6 / P5 Lemma EM, the case b = ∞** (write-up referee

# Changes: from the archived run to the manuscript

This file maps every result in `main.tex` to its source in the archived run
(`source/`), records the two referee reports for each proposition, and lists
every notation change, merged argument, correction and addition.

Archive: `source/` (archive label `zt-neutral`, archive commit
`ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba`); selected plan
`simplest@claude-opus-5-5` (`source/plan.md`, `source/plan.json`).
For every proposition PN, `source/props/PN/review-v1-0.json` is the review by
`claude-opus-5-5` and `source/props/PN/review-v1-1.json` the review by
`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`. Both reviewers passed all nine propositions in round 1
(severities: none or cosmetic). The assembly/integration reports are
`source/report/assembly-claude-opus-5-5.md`,
`source/report/assembly-codex-gpt-6.1-sol.md`,
`source/report/integration-*.json` and `source/report/integration.json`.

The theorem is stated with exactly the strength, ranges, hypotheses and
error terms of the plan's main theorem and of P9. The weight `f'(k)` and the
class of `f` are unchanged. No proposition is used outside its stated range.
No mathematical change was made beyond the local corrections listed in §4.
Each was identified by one of the following:

* the run's referees (`source/props/*/review-v1-*.json`);
* the operator audit recorded in `source/interventions.md` (2026-11-03 10:21),
  whose corrections are also named in the owner's "result" entry of 2026-11-03;
* the write-up referees, `claude-opus-5-5` and `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, after the
  run.

None of them weakens a statement or changes the main theorem. A few auxiliary
statements are stated slightly more strongly or more explicitly than in the
archived statement files. Each such case is taken from the archived proof or
proved in full in the manuscript, and is listed in §4a. One auxiliary lemma
(Lemma 2.6) received an extra hypothesis that holds in every application
(§4, item 19). That correction came from the write-up review, is not covered
by the owner's recorded decision, and is **flagged for Markus's
acknowledgement**.

**Write-up review files.** The write-up went through two review rounds
before this version. Both reports of each round are cited by round below:

* **Round 1** reports: these were `feedback/0.json` (`claude-opus-5-5`) and
  `feedback/1.json` (`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`) in the round-2 writer's workspace.
  They are *not* part of the present workspace, so references to them cannot
  be checked against the original files here. Each objection is restated
  inline below, in the round-2 writer's summary.
* **Round 2** reports: these are the files `feedback/0.json`
  (`claude-opus-5-5`, run `writeup-referee-zt-neutral-r2-0-…`) and
  `feedback/1.json` (`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, run
  `writeup-referee-zt-neutral-r2-1-…`) supplied with this version. Both
  verdicts are "revise". Both found no gap in the source argument and no
  change to the accepted mathematics. Their objections and the responses are
  in §8.

## 1. Map of results

## 3. Merged arguments

* **Tail bound** `Σ_{a>w} a^{-2} ≤ 2/w`: proved four times in the archive (P1 (i),
  P3 `(*)`, P4 (0), P5 (c)); stated once as Lemma 2.1 (P3's version, valid for all w > 0).
* **Counting integers in a residue class** (`N/L + θ`): P1 (i) and P3 Step 2 →
  Lemma 2.2.
* **Coprime pairs of squarefree numbers**: the Euler product
  `Σ μ(a)μ(b)/(ab)^2 = ∏_{p∤e}(1-2/p^2)` was derived twice by "local choices"
  (P1 proof (iv), P3 proof Step 4). Lemma 2.5 states it once. Its proof groups
  the pairs by n = ab, which turns the sum into the multiplicative series
  `Σ μ(n)2^{ω(n)} n^{-2} 1[(n,e)=1]`. This is the same computation in a
  shorter form.
* **Squarefree numbers coprime to r**: P4 (i) (count of Q(x)) and P4 (ii) Step 3
  (count of T_r) are the same estimate; Lemma 3.2 proves the general case, and
  Proposition 3.3(i) is its case r = 1. The constant `3√x` of P4 (i) is unchanged.
* **Facts on η, κ, A_0** scattered over P1, P2, P6 → Lemma 2.4.

## 4. Corrections (all local; no weakening of any statement)

1. **P1(iii), normalisation** (Sol review of P1, "other issues"; operator audit).
   The proof states `q·μ(d) g_d/d²·1[g_d | n] = ∏_{p|d} h(p)`, with an
   extraneous factor q. Corrected in Proposition 3.1(iii): `μ(d) g_d/d² 1[g_d|n]
   = ∏_{p|d} u(p)` and `q g(q,n) = Σ_d μ²(d) ∏_{p|d} u(p)`.
2. **P1(iii), convergence** (Sol review of P1, main objection, cosmetic;
   operator audit). The claim `Σ_p |h(p)| ≤ Σ_p p^{-2}` is false for p | q
   (e.g. q = n = 2). Corrected: `|u(p)| = p^{-2}` for p ∤ q, and `|u(p)| ≤ 1` for
   the finitely many p | q, so the series converges absolutely.
3. **P3 Step 3, constant** (Opus review of P3). The proof writes
   `2·(π²/6)·Σ e^{-2}(2e/z) ≤ (4π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`; the left side equals
   `(2π²/(3z)) Σ 1/e`. The original inequality was true but overestimated by a factor 2. The manuscript uses
   the correct value and the bound `7τ(m)/z` instead of `14τ(m)/z`. The final
   constant `(3 + 9C(ε))` replaces `2(1+τ*) + 1 + 14τ*`. Statement unchanged.
4. **P8 §3.4, endpoint k = 1** (Opus review of P8, cosmetic; operator audit;
   flagged as "P8 endpoint clarification" in `interventions.md`). The proof
   treats the closed first interval `[1, β]` as `(1-δ, β]`. That needs F to be defined and
   monotone left of 1, which fails e.g. for f = 3t − 1. Corrected by stating
   the counting lemma (Lemma 8.5) for arbitrary intervals (open, closed or
   half-open). Its proof only uses that `k_1 − e` and `k_n + e` lie outside the
   interval. The closed interval `[1, β]` is then covered directly, and the constant
   `3(2d−1) ≤ 6d` in eq. (8.10) (source eq. (3.9)) is unchanged.
5. **P8 §3.5, implicit error term** (Opus review of P8). The source writes
   `O(Y^{3/2} y^{-1/2})` for the term `(2/3)(Y^{3/2} − f(1)^{3/2})·O(y^{-1/2})`
   without saying where it comes from. The assembly display in §8.3 now shows
   it. The short-sum bound keeps the factor `(1 + log W)` (P8 (3.6)) explicitly,
   and it is absorbed by the choice `ε ≤ 1/8` (the source absorbs it into
   `E^{2ε}`). The final bound is unchanged.
6. **P8 §3.2(ii), constant dependence** (Opus review of P8). The bound
   `(2d)^{ω(n)} ≤ C n^ε` has a constant depending on d; this is now stated
   (`C(f, ε)`).
7. **P2, wording** (Opus review of P2). The parenthetical after (3) ("finitely
   many nonzero terms after the bracket is rewritten") is replaced by: the
   bracket vanishes for `q m_t(q) > x` (twice an empty sum), and each of the
   three series obtained by splitting it converges absolutely.
8. **P4 (i), wording** (Opus review of P4). "Every squarefree-indicator
   identity gives" → derived from `μ²(n) = Σ_{d²|n} μ(d)` (Lemma 3.2).
9. **P5(b), small s** (Opus review of P5). The two quantities both lie in
   `[0, Λ/4]`, so their difference is at most `Λ/4` (source: `Λ/2`). The constant
   `c_1 = 60` is kept.
10. **P9, real-variable hypothesis** (Opus review of P9). The step
    `f(k) ≤ f(y)` for real y uses `f'(t) ≥ 1` for all real `t ≥ 1`. This is
    now explicit in (1.1) and in §9. The convention `1 ≤ k ≤ y` (integers) is
    explicit in (1.2). The constants `c(ε/3)`, `c(f, ε/3)` and their
    combination are written out in §9.
11. **P9 remark on δ < 1/9** (Opus review of P9). Non-emptiness of the range
    holds for x > 1; stated so.
12. **P7, role of x ≥ 2** (Opus review of P7). Noted in the proof of
    Proposition 7.1 that x ≥ 2 is needed only for P3.
13. **P3, n ≥ 1** (Opus review of P3). C_x(m) counts positive n; explicit in
    eq. (4.1).
14. **P1(iii), sign of n** (Opus review of P1). Stated for squarefree `n ∈ ℕ`,
    the only case used.
15. **P5, citation "MV Thm B.5"** (Opus review of P5: not found in the
    supplied PDF). Appendix B of Montgomery–Vaughan is not in the supplied
    corpus. Its §1.3 refers to "Theorem B.5" for Euler–Maclaurin summation.
    The manuscript proves Lemma 2.6 directly and cites only MV §1.3 and
    Theorem 1.12 for comparison.
16. **Unused numerical notes in the proofs** (not reproduced):
    * P2: the proof's check agreed only to ~1e-3 because of truncation (Opus
      review); replaced by the exact self-test in `reproduce.py`
      (`identity_selftest`, agreement 4.8e-10).
    * P6: the tail estimate `A_0 x/(q·3000)` wrongly contains 1/q (Sol review),
      and the difference 92 at (10^6, 1) is a truncation artefact (Opus review).
    * P8: "ρ(p²) ≈ ρ(p)/p, exact for these squarefree f" is false for root
      counts (should be ρ(p²) = ρ(p) for unramified p); Sol review and Sol
      assembly report §5. Also flagged in the operator audit.
    * P1, P5: numerical sanity checks are not reproduced; P5's constants were
      checked by the referees.
17. **Remark 1.2 (range of part (ii))**. The plan says statement (a)/(ii)
    "remains meaningful up to f(y) ~ x". The manuscript states only what is
    proved: the error term of (ii) is of smaller order than `x^{1/2}Y^{3/2}`

    claimed.

    dropped because no statement from it is used. The plan named a 1949 paper
    of Mirsky on pairs of squarefree numbers from memory. Earlier versions of
    this write-up cited Mirsky, Bull. AMS 55 (1949), from
    `bibliography-candidates.json`, without having consulted it. The round-1
    write-up referee `claude-opus-5-5` (issue 7; objection in summary: the
    Mirsky citation was not verified against any supplied source) asked for
    this to be fixed, and the unverifiable historical attribution was dropped. Section 5 now quotes only what the
    supplied BGPVW (1998, §1) says about the related additive problem (see §5).
19. **Lemma 2.6 / P5 Lemma EM, the case b = ∞** — *correction introduced at
    the write-up stage; flagged for Markus's acknowledgement.* Raised by the
    round-1 write-up referee `codex:gpt-6.1-sol` (issue 1; objection in
    summary: the infinite-interval case of Lemma EM needs the convergence of
    `∫_a^∞ F`, which its stated hypotheses do not give). The round-2 referee
    `claude-opus-5-5` (`feedback/0.json`, issue 2) re-checked it and found
    the counterexample valid. That referee also found that every archived
    application satisfies the added hypothesis, so the issue is not a source
    gap. They asked that it be flagged here.
    P5 proof line 11 states the infinite-interval formula under `F, F' → 0`,
    `F'' ∈ L^1`. That is not enough: `G(u) = cos(log u)/u` on `[1, ∞)`
    satisfies these conditions, but its integral diverges. So the archived
    auxiliary lemma is false as stated in the case `b = ∞`. The manuscript
    adds the hypothesis that `∫_a^∞ G` converges, proves the limit passage,
    and notes that every application satisfies it: `G(u) = u^{-s}` with
    `Re s > 1` in Proposition 6.1(a) (P5 line 23), and
    `Φ(u) = Z/u² − Z²/u⁴` on `(T, ∞)` in Proposition 6.1(b) (P5 line 53). In
    both cases the integral converges absolutely.
    The argument of P5, and hence every proposition and the main theorem, is
    unaffected: the lemma is narrowed to the generality in which it is used.
    It is not a repair of a gap in the argument. However, it changes the
    statement of an auxiliary lemma of an approved proof, and it is not among
    the corrections recorded under the owner's 2026-11-03 decision (P1(iii),
    P8 endpoint, unused P6/P8 notes). It therefore awaits Markus's
    acknowledgement. If it is not acknowledged, the alternative is to state
    Lemma 2.6 for finite intervals only and to carry out the limit
    `b → ∞` separately in the two applications. That is the same argument
    in a different place.

    referee `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, issue 2; objection in summary: the sum of the

# Changes: from the archived run to the manuscript

This file maps every result in `main.tex` to its source in the archived run
(`source/`), records the two referee reports for each proposition, and lists
every notation change, merged argument, correction and addition.

Archive: `source/` (archive label `zt-neutral`, archive commit
`ed0aebaf461b602601856bf1b693fd76893d9aba`); selected plan
`simplest@claude-opus-5-5` (`source/plan.md`, `source/plan.json`).
For every proposition PN, `source/props/PN/review-v1-0.json` is the review by
`claude-opus-5-5` and `source/props/PN/review-v1-1.json` the review by
`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`. Both reviewers passed all nine propositions in round 1
(severities: none or cosmetic). The assembly/integration reports are
`source/report/assembly-claude-opus-5-5.md`,
`source/report/assembly-codex-gpt-6.1-sol.md`,
`source/report/integration-*.json` and `source/report/integration.json`.

The theorem is stated with exactly the strength, ranges, hypotheses and
error terms of the plan's main theorem and of P9. The weight `f'(k)` and the
class of `f` are unchanged. No proposition is used outside its stated range.
No mathematical change was made beyond the local corrections listed in §4.
Each was identified by one of the following:

* the run's referees (`source/props/*/review-v1-*.json`);
* the operator audit recorded in `source/interventions.md` (2026-11-03 10:21),
  whose corrections are also named in the owner's "result" entry of 2026-11-03;
* the write-up referees, `claude-opus-5-5` and `codex:gpt-6.1-sol`, after the
  run.

None of them weakens a statement or changes the main theorem. A few auxiliary
statements are stated slightly more strongly or more explicitly than in the
archived statement files. Each such case is taken from the archived proof or
proved in full in the manuscript, and is listed in §4a. One auxiliary lemma
(Lemma 2.6) received an extra hypothesis that holds in every application
(§4, item 19). That correction came from the write-up review, is not covered
by the owner's recorded decision, and is **flagged for Markus's
acknowledgement**.

**Write-up review files.** The write-up went through two review rounds
before this version. Both reports of each round are cited by round below:

* **Round 1** reports: these were `feedback/0.json` (`claude-opus-5-5`) and
  `feedback/1.json` (`codex:gpt-6.1-sol`) in the round-2 writer's workspace.
  They are *not* part of the present workspace, so references to them cannot
  be checked against the original files here. Each objection is restated

  change to the accepted mathematics. Their objections and the responses are
  in §8.

## 3. Merged arguments
